title: WordPress Developer (Technical) — Australian Digital Marketing Agency
description:
We're Viridi Marketing, a Perth-based digital marketing agency working with trade and service businesses across Australia. We're looking for a technical WordPress developer to join our subcontractor team on an ongoing basis — someone comfortable both building sites and managing the backend/hosting side.

A NOTE ON THE WORK
We don't do e-commerce. All our sites are simple lead-generation sites for service businesses (plumbers, electricians, home services, etc.) — the goal is either a lead form fill or a booking/call. Nothing complex.

We also plan and write all the content ourselves. Before any build starts, you'll receive a full content document — page by page, section by section, with all copy already written. Your job is to build exactly to that plan, not create or write content.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING
• Building 5–10 page WordPress websites for our clients, following our pre-written content and page plans
• Building and editing landing pages to support our Google Ads and SEO campaigns
• Liaising directly with our SEO team on website changes and technical SEO fixes
• Managing our Cloudways-hosted server environment — uploading/deploying sites, server-level configuration, troubleshooting when something breaks, and provisioning new servers when needed
• Diagnosing and fixing plugin conflicts or backend issues on client sites

We use an automated tool for routine backups, updates, and uptime monitoring — this role is about the technical work those tools can't do: server management, troubleshooting, and integrations.

TIMEZONE
We're based in Perth, Australia (AWST). We need someone who can work at least partially within or close to our hours — Eastern Europe or the Philippines work well for us. We'd prefer to avoid US/American working hours, as the overlap with our team is too limited.

WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU
• Portfolio or links to recent WordPress sites you've built (we'll also share a few of our own recent builds for reference)
• Experience managing hosting environments — Cloudways specifically is a plus
• Experience with API/CRM integrations (GoHighLevel experience is a bonus)
• How you'd typically price a 5–10 page site build (rough range is fine — happy to discuss further on a call)
• Your usual hourly rate for ongoing edits, troubleshooting, and server management

This is an ongoing subcontractor role, not a one-off project — we're looking for someone to build a working relationship with over time.

title: Senior WordPress Developer/Agency — Financial Services Website Redesign & SEO-Preserving Migration
description:
Project Overview

Kram Capital Group is a nationwide commercial loan brokerage headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.

We are seeking an experienced senior WordPress developer, boutique agency, or specialized development team to redesign and modernize our existing WordPress website.

This is NOT simply a website reskin or theme installation project.

Our existing website is built on an outdated WordPress environment and needs significant modernization. However, the website has accumulated valuable organic Google rankings, indexed pages and third-party backlinks over many years.

Therefore, the successful candidate must have experience redesigning established WordPress websites without unnecessarily damaging existing SEO performance.

Primary Objectives

The project includes:

Modernize/rebuild the existing WordPress environment
Create a sophisticated new UI/UX
Improve mobile experience
Improve site speed and Core Web Vitals
Preserve important existing URLs and SEO equity
Improve site navigation/information architecture
Improve lead-generation and conversion capabilities
Integrate forms with our existing technology
Build reusable templates for future SEO/content expansion
Improve security and maintainability
Design Direction

We want KramCapital.com to look and feel like a modern:

Commercial Finance / Private Credit / Commercial Real Estate / Fintech Platform

We do not want the website to resemble a residential mortgage template or generic WordPress theme.

The website must appropriately represent financing transactions ranging from small-balance investor loans to multimillion-dollar commercial transactions.

SEO Migration Is Critical

This is one of the most important requirements.

KramCapital.com currently has pages that rank organically for commercially valuable financing searches and have accumulated third-party backlinks.

The selected developer may not arbitrarily change URLs, delete pages or restructure existing SEO assets.

We expect:

Existing URL audit
URL preservation strategy
Redirect mapping where necessary
Metadata migration
Canonical implementation
Internal-link preservation/improvement
Schema implementation
XML sitemap
Search Console validation
Pre-launch crawl
Post-launch crawl
Broken-link/404 testing

We may have a separate SEO specialist involved in reviewing the migration.

You must be comfortable collaborating with an outside SEO professional.

Website Architecture

The new website will support major financing categories including:

Commercial Real Estate

SBA & Business Financing

DSCR Investment Property

Short-Term Rental / Airbnb

Hotels & Hospitality

Commercial Bridge

Construction

Multifamily

Industrial/Warehouse

Self Storage

Office

Retail

Foreign National Financing

The architecture must allow us to add substantial new SEO content without custom programming every time a page is created.

Conversion & Integrations

We want to improve the website from an informational site into a stronger digital loan-origination platform.

Requirements may include:

Multi-step qualification forms
Conditional form logic
LendingWise CRM integration
Calendly
GA4
Google Tag Manager
Google Search Console
UTM/source attribution
Future integration with third-party lead-generation technology

The architecture should also support future financing calculators.

Technical Requirements

Strong experience required with:

WordPress
PHP
Responsive development
Modern WordPress architecture
Staging environments
WordPress migrations
Core Web Vitals
Technical SEO
Security
Backups
CDN/caching
APIs/webhooks
GA4/GTM

We prefer clean architecture with limited unnecessary plugin dependence.

Ownership

Kram Capital Group must receive full administrative access and ownership of all custom work created specifically for the project upon final payment.

We do not want to be permanently dependent upon the selected developer to operate the website.

Who We Are Looking For

We are interested in:

Senior WordPress developers
Boutique WordPress agencies
Experienced international development teams
U.S.-based or international candidates

Location is less important than quality, communication, accountability and demonstrated results.

Financial-services, commercial real-estate, banking, lending or fintech website experience is strongly preferred.

Application Requirements

Please include:

Five WordPress websites you personally or your team developed.
At least two examples of established websites you redesigned where preserving organic SEO rankings was important.
Briefly explain how you handle URL preservation and redirects during a redesign.
Describe your experience improving Core Web Vitals and page speed.
Describe your experience integrating WordPress forms with CRMs through APIs/webhooks.
Identify who will actually perform the work and where your development team is located.
Provide your estimated fixed-price range for a project of this scope.
Provide your estimated timeline.
Important Screening Question

Please answer this question in your proposal:

If an existing KramCapital.com page ranks strongly for a valuable Google search term and has backlinks from authoritative third-party websites, how would you redesign that page without unnecessarily jeopardizing its rankings and backlink equity?

Please be specific.

Generic responses such as "we follow SEO best practices" will not be considered sufficient.

Selection Process

We will review initial applications and select approximately 5–10 qualified candidates.

Selected candidates will receive a more detailed Website Redesign & WordPress Modernization RFP covering:

Full technical requirements
SEO migration requirements
Information architecture
Conversion requirements
Deliverables
Pricing schedule
Project milestones
Vendor scoring criteria

We expect to interview approximately three finalists before selecting a development partner.

This is a significant project for an established commercial finance company. We are looking for a development partner capable of building a platform that will support our next stage of digital growth.
coverLetter:
Hi! Regarding your key screening question: if an existing KramCapital.com page ranks strongly and holds valuable backlinks, I would never change its URL slug or alter the core on-page content hierarchy unless strictly necessary. If a redesign requires a new URL structure, I implement a 1:1 mapping using 301 redirects, preserve exact title tags, meta descriptions, and schema markup, and keep internal link anchors intact. If the URL remains the same, we update the UI/UX around the existing content safely in a staging environment before pushing live.

As a senior WordPress developer, I specialize in modernizing legacy sites with clean architecture (minimal plugin bloat), achieving top-tier Core Web Vitals, and executing complex SEO-preserving migrations. I also build scalable custom templates using ACF and Gutenberg for easy content expansion, and integrate advanced multi-step forms with external CRMs via APIs/webhooks. 

You can review a recent complex build here: https://www.cchpca.0rg/ (or waapple.org). 

I perform all development personally to ensure uncompromising quality. Let's connect in chat to discuss your scope and timeline!

title: WordPress Website Development
description:
Senior WordPress/PHP Developer Needed to Implement Medicare Preventive Services Questionnaire and PDF Reporting Plugin

Project Description

We are developing a customer-facing Five Year Road Map to Medicare Preventive Services.

We already have an initial custom WordPress plugin package, questionnaire structure, preventive-services scheduling logic, branded report design, official logo and example PDF reports. We need an experienced WordPress/PHP developer to review, test, correct, complete and deploy this system on our GoDaddy-hosted WordPress website.

This is not primarily a website-design or Elementor project. The main work involves custom WordPress plugin development, backend calculations, PDF generation, secure data handling, email delivery and production deployment.

How the System Should Work

A customer visits a page on our WordPress website.
The customer completes a multi-step Medicare preventive-services questionnaire.
The system evaluates the answers using programmed eligibility and scheduling rules.
The system calculates a personalized five-year preventive-services schedule.
A branded PDF report is generated automatically.
The customer receives an email with a secure report-download link.
Authorized staff can review submissions and reports through a WordPress administrative dashboard.

Existing Materials

We will provide:

The existing WordPress plugin ZIP
The questionnaire and conditional-question structure
The initial Medicare scheduling engine
The official logo and brand colors
The approved one-page report format
Example completed reports
Instructions describing the intended workflow
Test customer profiles and expected outputs

The selected developer must be comfortable reviewing and improving existing code rather than rebuilding the entire project without first evaluating what is already available.

Required Development Work

Review the existing plugin code and architecture
Install it on a GoDaddy staging WordPress site
Correct PHP, JavaScript, database or WordPress compatibility issues
Complete the questionnaire and conditional-question behavior
Validate form fields and sanitize all submitted information
Review and correct the deterministic scheduling calculations
Ensure dates, age thresholds, frequencies and service histories calculate correctly
Complete server-side branded PDF generation
Ensure the official logo and report table display correctly
Configure secure report storage and download links
Configure WordPress transactional email delivery
Configure authenticated SMTP and test delivery
Complete the WordPress administrative report dashboard
Add appropriate administrative permissions and access restrictions
Create error handling and logging
Test the website on desktop, tablet and mobile devices
Document installation, configuration, backup and update procedures
Deploy the approved version from staging to production

Security and Privacy Requirements

The questionnaire may collect individually identifiable health-related information. The developer must follow secure development practices, including:

HTTPS throughout the workflow
WordPress nonces and server-side validation
Input sanitization and output escaping
Prepared database queries
High-entropy report-access tokens
Role-based administrative access
Administrative multi-factor authentication
Protection against direct access to stored reports
Secure backups
Data-retention and deletion controls
Audit or activity logging
No advertising pixels on questionnaire or report-download pages
No exposure of submitted information in URLs, analytics tools or ordinary WordPress logs

Experience working with HIPAA-sensitive, healthcare, insurance or financial-information systems is strongly preferred. The developer should not claim that the system is “HIPAA compliant” merely because basic security controls are present. Legal and compliance review will be handled separately.

Required Technical Experience

Applicants should have demonstrable experience with:

Custom WordPress plugin development
PHP 8.0 or later
WordPress coding and security standards
MySQL and custom WordPress database tables
JavaScript and AJAX
WordPress shortcodes
WordPress administrative pages
WordPress email and SMTP
Server-side PDF generation
Secure file storage and downloads
GoDaddy WordPress hosting or GoDaddy cPanel
Staging-to-production deployment
Git or another version-control system
Responsive front-end development

Preferred Experience

Healthcare or insurance applications
Health-related questionnaires
Eligibility or rules engines
Automated document generation
Transactional email systems
Privacy-by-design development
Accessibility testing
WordPress penetration testing or security hardening

Required Deliverables

Technical review of the existing plugin
Written list of required corrections
Working questionnaire installed on staging
Validated scheduling engine
Automatic branded PDF generation
Secure customer report delivery
Working email and SMTP configuration
Administrative dashboard
Completed test plan with results
Production deployment on GoDaddy
Source code and final installable plugin ZIP
Installation and administrator documentation
A short post-deployment support period for defects

Testing Requirements

The developer must test multiple profiles, including:

A new Medicare Part B member
A long-time Medicare member
A Medicare Advantage member
An Original Medicare member
Male and female screening profiles
A current smoker
A former smoker
A person who never smoked
A person with diabetes or prediabetes
A customer with unknown service history
Multiple colorectal-screening methods
Missing or incomplete vaccination history
A roadmap beginning in the middle of a calendar year

For each profile, the developer must compare the generated report with the expected results we provide.

Project Approach

We prefer a milestone-based project:

Milestone 1: Code review and staging installation
Milestone 2: Questionnaire and calculation engine
Milestone 3: PDF generation and report delivery
Milestone 4: Administrative dashboard and security controls
Milestone 5: Testing, GoDaddy production deployment and documentation

Do not make production changes before the staging version is reviewed and approved.

When Applying

Please answer the following questions:

Describe two custom WordPress plugins you personally developed.
Have you created server-side PDFs from WordPress data? Which PDF library or method did you use?
Have you deployed a custom WordPress plugin on GoDaddy?
How would you protect customer reports from unauthorized access?
How would you prevent questionnaire information from appearing in analytics or logs?
How would you test a rules engine that calculates future dates?
What information would you need before configuring SMTP?
Have you worked with healthcare, insurance or other sensitive customer information?
Will you personally perform the work, or will it be assigned to another developer?
Are you willing to provide all source code, documentation and deployment instructions?

Please include examples of relevant custom plugin work. General WordPress design portfolios without custom PHP/plugin examples will not be sufficient.
coverLetter:
Hi! I have extensive experience building custom WordPress plugins and handling secure, data-driven applications, and I am ready to review and complete your Medicare roadmap system.

Regarding your questions:
1. I’ve developed complex plugins for membership management and custom API-driven booking systems.
2. I frequently use TCPDF and Dompdf for server-side PDF generation from dynamic data.
3. Yes, I have deployed numerous custom plugins on GoDaddy environments, including staging-to-production workflows.
4. I protect reports using high-entropy, expiring download tokens and directory-level security.
5. I prevent data leakage by sanitizing inputs before logging and excluding sensitive fields from all analytics/debug hooks.
6. I test rules engines by unit-testing the calculation logic against your provided test profiles.
7. For SMTP, I need your host, port, authentication credentials, and encryption type.
8. Yes, I have experience with secure, sensitive data handling. I will perform all work personally and provide full documentation and source code.

Could we schedule a brief chat to discuss the existing plugin architecture?

title: WordPress Website Migration and Complete Ownership Transfer
description:
WordPress Website Migration and Complete Business Ownership Transfer

Painter Ready is a residential and commercial painting company in Chattanooga, Tennessee. We need an experienced WordPress migration specialist to move our existing website from infrastructure controlled by a former service provider into accounts owned and controlled directly by our company.

This is primarily a technical migration, ownership-transfer, testing, and documentation project. It is not a website redesign.

Current Environment

The website appears to use:

* WordPress
* Divi theme or builder
* Contact Form 7
* SiteGround or similar hosting controlled by the current provider
* Google Tag Manager
* Google Analytics 4
* Google Search Console
* Google Ads conversion tracking
* Domain, DNS, SSL, email-routing, security, and plugin dependencies that must be inventoried and verified

The exact ownership and configuration of some components remain unresolved. The selected freelancer must be comfortable investigating an incomplete or poorly documented environment and identifying what access is still needed before migration begins.

Primary Objective

Successfully migrate the existing Painter Ready website into company-owned accounts without losing website content, functionality, search visibility, lead delivery, email service, analytics data, or conversion tracking.

All new accounts, services, recovery methods, and administrator access must be owned by Painter Ready. The freelancer will receive named individual access and must not register business assets in the freelancer’s own name or account.

Scope of Work

Milestone 1 — Technical Audit and Migration Plan

Before making changes, the freelancer will:

* Review all access and materials supplied by the current provider.
* Confirm WordPress administrator access.
* Identify the current hosting provider and hosting-control-panel access.
* Identify the domain registrar, registrant, DNS provider, nameservers, and renewal status.
* Inventory the WordPress version, PHP version, database, themes, plugins, licenses, users, custom code, redirects, cron jobs, and integrations.
* Identify all active recurring services and costs associated with the website.
* Document the current SSL, CDN, firewall, caching, backup, malware protection, and security configuration.
* Review Contact Form 7 forms and determine how form notifications are delivered.
* Document SMTP, email-routing, MX, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC dependencies before any DNS changes.
* Inventory Google Tag Manager, GA4, Search Console, and Google Ads tracking.
* Investigate possible duplicate GTM containers and duplicate Google Ads scripts.
* Identify missing access, licenses, credentials, or dependencies that could prevent a complete migration.
* Deliver a written migration plan, risk list, access checklist, rollback plan, and firm price for the remaining milestones.

No migration or DNS changes may begin until the audit is complete and Painter Ready approves the migration plan.

Milestone 2 — Backup and Staging Migration

The freelancer will:

* Create and verify a complete independent backup of all WordPress files and the database.
* Preserve wp-config.php, uploads, media, theme files, child themes, plugin settings, redirects, and custom code.
* Create the new website environment in company-owned hosting.
* Configure the new environment using appropriate PHP, database, SSL, caching, security, and backup settings.
* Migrate the complete website to a staging location.
* Preserve the existing URL structure, page titles, metadata, schema, sitemap, robots directives, canonical URLs, and redirects.
* Confirm that licensed themes and plugins can legally continue to operate after separation from the former provider.
* Identify any license that must be replaced and obtain approval before purchasing or substituting anything.
* Test the staging website on desktop and mobile.
* Check every page, menu, image, button, link, form, redirect, and downloadable asset.
* Confirm that the staging environment is blocked from search-engine indexing.

Milestone 3 — Lead Flow, Email, and Tracking Validation

The website’s lead flow is business-critical. The freelancer will:

* Verify all displayed business contact information against the information Painter Ready provides privately after hiring.
* Verify that estimate forms capture, at minimum, name, phone number, ZIP code, and service requested.
* Preserve or properly configure optional email and project-description fields.
* Verify that form submissions reach the correct Painter Ready recipient.
* Configure dependable authenticated email delivery if needed.
* Verify the customer confirmation or auto-response.
* Configure a reliable form-success or thank-you state.
* Ensure conversions count successful submissions only—not button clicks, page visits, or failed submissions.
* Remove or correct duplicate GTM and Google Ads tracking only after documenting the existing installation.
* Confirm that GA4, Google Tag Manager, Google Ads, and Search Console are connected to company-owned accounts.
* Perform live test submissions on desktop and mobile and provide evidence of successful delivery and conversion recording.
* Avoid disrupting email associated with the painter-ready.com domain.

Milestone 4 — Production Cutover and Verification

The freelancer will:

* Schedule the cutover to minimize disruption.
* Create a fresh backup immediately before cutover.
* Update DNS only after confirming that all required email records and website settings are documented.
* Install and verify SSL.
* Confirm that the production website loads correctly with and without “www.”
* Check for mixed content, broken links, missing images, PHP errors, console errors, redirect loops, and indexing problems.
* Re-test forms, email delivery, analytics, conversions, phone links, buttons, and mobile functionality.
* Monitor the website after launch and correct migration-related problems.
* Maintain a documented rollback path throughout the cutover.
* Coordinate retention of the former hosting environment for a short verification period when the existing provider permits it.

Milestone 5 — Ownership and Documentation Handoff

Before final payment, the freelancer will provide:

* A complete inventory of all website-related systems and accounts.
* Confirmation that Painter Ready owns the hosting, domain, DNS, analytics, tracking, and recovery methods.
* A list of all company administrators and their access levels.
* Confirmation that MFA and company-controlled recovery methods are enabled where supported.
* A list of all active plugins, licenses, renewals, subscriptions, and recurring costs.
* Final backup files and instructions for restoring the website.
* DNS and email-record documentation.
* Analytics and conversion-tracking documentation.
* A list of any unresolved risks, inaccessible assets, or dependencies on the former provider.
* A short recorded walkthrough of the new hosting, backups, WordPress administration, and recovery process.
* Removal of temporary freelancer access after Painter Ready confirms completion.

Important Requirements

* Do not redesign the website.
* Do not change the existing URL structure without written approval.
* Do not make unapproved content, SEO, branding, pricing, or service changes.
* Do not purchase hosting, plugins, themes, domains, or other subscriptions without prior written approval.
* Do not transfer or recreate domain email records without first documenting the existing MX, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configuration.
* Do not perform the live cutover without a verified backup and rollback plan.
* Do not remove the former provider’s access until Painter Ready confirms that the migrated website, forms, email delivery, and tracking are working.
* Do not place company assets in accounts owned by the freelancer or another agency.
* All passwords and sensitive information must be transferred through a secure credential-sharing method, not ordinary email or Upwork messages.

Required Experience

Applicants must demonstrate experience with:

* Complete WordPress website migrations
* Divi websites
* SiteGround or comparable managed WordPress hosting
* Hosting-control panels, SFTP, databases, and phpMyAdmin
* Domain registrars and DNS management
* Cloudflare or comparable DNS/CDN services
* SSL certificates, caching, firewalls, and WordPress security
* Contact Form 7 and authenticated SMTP delivery
* MX, SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records
* Google Tag Manager
* Google Analytics 4
* Google Search Console
* Google Ads conversion tracking
* WordPress backups and disaster recovery
* SEO-safe migrations and redirect validation
* Troubleshooting websites with incomplete access or documentation

Preferred Qualifications

* At least five completed WordPress migrations with client feedback
* Upwork Job Success Score of 90% or higher
* Demonstrated experience moving websites away from agency-controlled hosting
* Experience transferring sites while preserving domain-based email
* Experience identifying duplicate or broken analytics and conversion tracking
* Strong written documentation and clear communication

Proposal Instructions

Please begin your proposal with the words “Painter Ready Migration” so we know you read the entire scope.

Your proposal must include:

1. Two or three examples of comparable WordPress migrations you personally completed.
2. A short explanation of how you prevent DNS changes from interrupting business email.
3. Your approach when the existing provider supplies incomplete access or documentation.
4. The backup and rollback process you use.
5. How you validate forms, SMTP delivery, GA4, GTM, Search Console, and Google Ads conversions after migration.
6. Your proposed fixed price and milestone breakdown.
7. Your estimated duration after complete access is received.
8. Any assumptions or exclusions in your price.
9. Whether you personally perform the work or use subcontractors.
10. Your availability for limited post-launch support.

Please do not submit a generic proposal or propose a complete redesign. We are looking for a careful migration specialist who understands ownership, DNS, email continuity, lead tracking, documentation, and rollback—not merely someone who can install WordPress.

title: Senior WordPress Plugin Developer: Reusable Gallery with Connected Treatment-Page Results
description:
Medstar Media is hiring an experienced WordPress plugin developer to build and maintain a reusable before-and-after gallery for medical and aesthetic practice websites.
We need one installable plugin that our team can configure and brand across multiple websites. Practice staff must be able to add sections, procedures, photographs, and cases without developer assistance. The first release will be piloted on two websites before additional layouts are added.

We will supply requirements and visual references. We expect you to recommend the implementation, identify missing requirements and risks, and explain your architecture, migration approach, testing, security, performance, and fixed-price milestones. Relevant product experience and technical judgment are essential.

FIRST-RELEASE SCOPE
Deliver one clean, neutral default layout for each of these three page types:

Main gallery directory organized by sections, categories, and procedures.
Procedure gallery showing the cases associated with a procedure.
Individual case page with photographs, optional details, and a configurable consultation call to action.
The first release includes the full data model, settings framework, and licensing/update mechanism. Additional page layouts are planned for a later release. Demonstrate how a new layout can be added without rebuilding the data model, settings system, or existing templates.
There is no separate Figma or bespoke design phase. Build a polished neutral default using the reference material linked below. Colors, fonts, corner radius, spacing, and other agreed brand settings must be adjustable without editing templates. Client-specific directory redesigns and branding implementation are handled by Medstar after delivery.

IMAGE PRESENTATION

A separate image-pair setting must control side-by-side versus vertically stacked presentation, independently of the page layout.
Provide independent desktop and mobile values for that setting. Stacked means Before above After.
Support separate before/after files, a single pre-combined image, and multiple labeled angles.
Preserve the full content and proportions of combined images. Do not split a combined image or imply its arrangement can be changed without separate source files.
Every applicable view must handle a combined image with no patient details gracefully, without empty panels, broken controls, or distorted photographs.
Include an accessible enlarged photo viewer with before/after labels, multiple-angle navigation, keyboard controls, focus management, and a mobile layout. Preserve full image proportions in the viewer.
Support square preview tiles using a staff-selected safe crop or a contained image. Do not crop away clinically important results or distort combined images.
Side-by-side and stacked comparisons are the base delivery. Quote a draggable comparison slider as a separate optional addition, disabled by default and requiring approval. It must support suitable separate image pairs, keyboard controls, and a non-drag alternative. Combined files must retain their normal presentation. Explain source-image requirements; do not promise automatic alignment or splitting.

DATA AND STAFF WORKFLOWS
One record represents one patient case. Preserve these capabilities regardless of which fields are displayed publicly:

Editable case title with automatic numbering.
Before image, after image, or combined image; additional labeled angles.
Optional description, age range, gender, procedures/sessions performed, time between photographs, and provider.
Featured-case selection, sensitive-content flag, consent-on-file confirmation, and consent reference.
Staff-managed sections, categories, procedures, and providers. Support arbitrary numbers of each and explain their relationships and handling of cases associated with multiple procedures.
Dedicated Gallery menu and a restricted Gallery Manager role with the upload and editing permissions necessary for this workflow.
Bulk image upload with procedure assignment and an explicit way to group images into cases and angles.
Manual ordering within a procedure, plus featured-first and date-based ordering.
A simple guided workflow that a nontechnical user can complete in approximately two minutes for a prepared, single-pair case.
Allow each website to require procedure, provider, age range, time since treatment, and description before publishing, while other websites can leave these fields optional. Public case labels must use anonymous identifiers, not patient names.

CONNECTED RESULTS ON WEBSITE PAGES

Provide an Elementor-compatible block, widget, or shortcode usable on treatment pages, service-line landing pages, and the homepage. Also support embedding without Elementor.
Store each case once. Embeds reference the central case record and never require staff to maintain duplicate photographs or descriptions on individual pages.
Let staff select and order featured cases per procedure, with a configurable display count such as the top five. Also support a separately curated homepage selection such as three cases across different services.
Allow an embed to select one or multiple procedures and optionally a service line and provider. Grouped pages must be able to show cases from several treatment brands without duplicating a case assigned to multiple procedures.
Staff-selected cases are the default. Automatic latest-case selection may be offered as an explicit setting, but must not silently replace curated choices. With too few eligible cases, display only the available cases; hide an empty results block cleanly.
Changes to case images, descriptions, selections, order, publication status, consent, or sensitivity must update affected embeds and galleries. Include cache invalidation for supported WordPress/page-cache configurations, document update timing and any cache limitations, and test with caching enabled.
Provide a relevant View All Results link to the matching gallery selection. Enforce publication, consent, and sensitive-content rules in every embed.

CONSENT AND SENSITIVE CONTENT
Consent-on-file confirmation is mandatory. An empty or false value must block publishing through all supported editing, bulk, API, import, and scheduled-publishing paths. Imported content must never be treated as consented merely because it was previously public.
Support an internal consent reference and an administrative audit of missing confirmation or references. Propose how to store references privately; real consent documents must not be exposed through public media URLs or public API responses. We prefer a reference to a practice-held record rather than storing signed patient documents in WordPress.
Sensitive cases require configurable click-to-reveal warnings wherever their images appear, including directory representative images, featured strips, case cards, related cases, and detail pages. Clearly document the limits of visual blur and right-click deterrents; neither is access control or a guarantee against downloading public images.
Support a website-level gallery-only policy for sensitive cases: treatment pages and other embeds must show an approved safe link/placeholder leading to the gallery instead of revealing the sensitive photographs inline. Apply the same policy to homepage and service-line results. The gallery warning must support editable 18+ acknowledgment and results-vary wording. Confirm acknowledgment duration at the requirements milestone. This is a viewing acknowledgment, not verified age identification or a contact-information form.
Use a safe preview before acknowledgment and defer sensitive full-image requests until reveal. Do not describe this behavior as private media protection: public media URLs may remain accessible directly, and images can be copied after viewing. Patient publication consent is separate from the visitor's viewing acknowledgment; a visitor click never establishes patient consent.

SETTINGS AND FRONTEND BEHAVIOR
Provide a coherent settings interface covering:

Extensible layout selection, brand styling, image-pair arrangement, gallery base slug, warning text, and CTA text/destination.
Directory intro, case counts, empty-procedure visibility, featured-case strip, and section search.
Optional filters for service line, procedure, provider, age range, and gender, disabled by default per website. Support a service line to procedure to provider filtering sequence with valid dependent options, clear/reset controls, and usable mobile controls. Demonstrate both filters-enabled and filters-disabled configurations. Cases and providers may belong to multiple service lines.
Sort order, cases per page, pagination options, description previews, provider display, and breadcrumbs.
Individual visibility controls for case details, previous/next navigation within a procedure, related cases, and CTA display.
Social sharing disabled by default and optional download/right-click deterrents that do not interfere with accessibility.
Per-section indexing controls, including a documented policy for cases belonging to more than one section.
The feature list above forms the baseline for pricing. Reducing the number of page layouts does not silently remove settings or data capabilities. Explicitly list any proposed deferrals, alternatives, and exclusions before the build price is agreed.

GALLERY ENGAGEMENT
Provide documented, optional events for gallery filtering, case opening, sensitive-content acknowledgment, and gallery consultation clicks, including events from embedded results. Connect to a website's approved analytics setup without installing duplicate tracking tags. Do not transmit patient names, descriptions, photographs, consent references, visitor contact information, or sensitive clinical details. Agree on permitted event fields and consent behavior before implementation. Analytics must not be required for the gallery to work.

LICENSING, UPDATES, AND CLIENT HANDOFF
Medstar needs to control initial activation because not every client agreement includes the gallery. Once legitimately activated, the gallery must continue operating if a license is removed, revoked, expires, or the licensing service becomes unavailable. Public rendering must never depend on a successful remote check.
Removing a license ends access to Medstar-provided updates, security-fix downloads, and support. It must not disable the existing gallery or its content-management functions. Include an entitlement option for permanent use; do not assume this automatically includes lifetime updates or support.
Propose the licensing service, admin controls, authenticated update delivery, and signed/local activation evidence needed to implement this. Include setup and documentation in the quote, disclose operating costs and dependencies, and distinguish brand-new unauthorized installations from previously authorized websites. Describe behavior during outages, temporary deactivation/reactivation, domain changes, staging clones, and a hosting transfer. These lifecycle rules must be agreed at the first milestone before implementation.
Existing client galleries must not acquire a remote kill switch. No patient content may be transmitted to the licensing service. Any external service or paid dependency requires written approval. The approved licensing/update service is an exception to the original draft's prohibition on external APIs and license servers; gallery content must remain local to the website.

TECHNICAL DELIVERY AND VERIFICATION

Deliver an installable plugin, source code, build instructions, and documentation in Medstar-owned accounts and a repository.
Work with Elementor while allowing installation on a clean WordPress site without Elementor. Declare tested WordPress, PHP, theme, and dependency versions.
ACF Pro is our preferred available foundation. Explain dependency handling, licensing, updates, and behavior during a client handoff. Alternatives require a clear justification and approval.
Provide extension points for future layouts and client overrides, scoped styles, translation-ready strings, and upgrade-safe data migrations.
Preserve recoverable case data and media on deactivation and uninstall, with documented export/recovery instructions.
Provide responsive image sizing, appropriate lazy loading, WebP/fallback handling, and minimal gallery assets on unrelated pages.
Test a procedure containing at least 60 cases. Propose measurable loading, responsiveness, and resource-use targets with stated devices, network, hosting, and cache conditions before development.
Provide clean URLs, canonical handling for multi-procedure cases, editable alt text, suitable structured data, and CSV redirect-map import with validation.
Verify keyboard operation, focus behavior, screen-reader labeling, mobile layouts, and agreed desktop/mobile browser coverage.
Test permissions, private metadata exposure, input validation, output escaping, upload handling, import safety, and licensing/update security.
Supply automated tests, a repeatable manual test plan, results, and known limitations. Medstar will independently verify delivery against agreed acceptance criteria.
Demonstrate one central edit updating multiple embedded results blocks, grouped-procedure deduplication, empty/fewer-than-requested cases, dependent filters, full-image viewing, and sensitive gallery-only rules on desktop and mobile. Verify removing a case or withdrawing its publication consent also removes it from cached gallery and embedded results under the supported cache configuration.

PILOT CONTEXT AND BOUNDARIES
Pilot A has two sections and approximately 149 existing cases with 248 image entries, many of them combined images. Preserve sensitive flags and support cases without descriptions. Filters will be off.
Pilot B has three practice divisions and more than 70 procedure pages, with staff preparing their own photographs and case descriptions. Filters will be off.
An additional configuration must support three service lines with filters enabled, connected treatment-page results, curated homepage results, required case details, and sensitive cases restricted to the gallery. Its final case volume and production rollout are to be confirmed; do not assume it is an additional included production migration.
Build and test with placeholder content on a Medstar-owned sandbox. You will not receive live client access, patient photographs, or signed consent records. Propose and document a migration approach using synthetic examples, including safe reruns, validation, and rollback. Actual client-data migration, client-specific migration scripts, production installation, and bespoke client styling are separate Medstar work unless separately commissioned. The reusable CSV redirect importer is included in this build.

REFERENCE MATERIAL
The visual and functional reference examples are collected in this Google Drive document:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i-59hs-E3x9lHfHlMV4coiQZYHtmvuuY2gKBW43oX4U/edit
Use these examples to understand the expected navigation, case presentation, and execution quality. They are references only. No source-code audit or reuse is assumed. Do not copy proprietary code, branding, written content, or patient assets.

PROPOSED FIXED-PRICE MILESTONES

Requirements validation, architecture, explicit inclusions/exclusions, licensing lifecycle, maintenance/dependency plan, and measurable acceptance tests. Confirm the final build price before implementation. No separate design phase.
Data model, staff administration, roles, consent enforcement, settings framework, and image handling.
Three default page layouts, connected results embeds, responsive image arrangements, enlarged photo viewer, dependent filters, sensitive-content placement rules, licensing service, and update delivery.
Engagement events, verification, security/performance/accessibility fixes, cache-update checks, redirect importer, documented migration approach, installable package, and handoff.

SEPARATELY PRICED OPTIONS

Draggable before-and-after comparison slider, subject to the image and accessibility requirements above.
A later video gallery, with hosting, playback, captions, consent, sensitive-content handling, and migration requirements defined before pricing is finalized. It is not included in the first photo-gallery release.
Contact-information collection to unlock images, verified age checks, and authenticated private-media delivery are not part of the click-to-view warning scope. Do not include them implicitly.
Payments are tied to accepted milestones. Identify omissions and assumptions before scope approval. Corrections needed to meet agreed requirements are defects, not new features. Requests outside the agreed scope require an approved change estimate.
Include a proposed post-delivery defect warranty and separately price ongoing compatibility maintenance, security fixes, support response times, and licensing/update-service operation. Do not assume ongoing maintenance is included indefinitely or automatically assigned to Medstar's reviewer.
Medstar must receive the source and rights necessary to maintain, modify, install, and hand off the system without dependence on the original contractor. Custom work product is assigned to Medstar on final payment; disclose all third-party licenses and dependencies before approval.

PLEASE INCLUDE IN YOUR APPLICATION

One reusable WordPress plugin you personally built and maintained, where it was deployed, and your role.
One frontend you personally implemented so we can assess the quality of your default layouts.
Your proposed architecture, dependencies, and approach to adding layouts later without rebuilding the system.
Your migration, licensing/handoff, testing, security, and performance plan, including gaps you see in this brief.
A fixed-price quote by milestone, timeline, assumptions, exclusions, warranty, and a separate maintenance proposal. Include licensing infrastructure and recurring costs. Identify the incremental cost of connected results embeds, enhanced filtering/viewing, and engagement events. Price optional sliders and later video support separately so Medstar can approve them independently.
We value applicants who can explain tradeoffs and deliver a maintainable product that another developer can support.

title: Senior WordPress Developer - ACF Pro, PageSpeed, PHP & Technical SEO
description:
# Senior WordPress Developer - ACF Pro, PageSpeed, PHP & Technical SEO

We are looking for an experienced **WordPress developer** who is strong in custom WordPress development, Advanced Custom Fields (ACF), frontend implementation, performance optimisation and technical SEO.

This is not primarily a page-builder role.

We need someone who is comfortable working with an existing WordPress website, building custom templates and components, troubleshooting issues, improving performance, and creating a WordPress backend that is easy for non-technical team members to manage.

## What You Will Work On

Typical work will include:

* Developing custom WordPress pages and templates from HTML, Figma or existing designs
* Building maintainable content structures using **Advanced Custom Fields (ACF / ACF Pro)**
* Creating ACF Groups, Repeaters, conditional fields and structured content components
* Developing clean PHP, HTML, CSS and JavaScript
* Working with existing themes and WordPress codebases
* Troubleshooting PHP, CSS, JavaScript, plugin and WordPress issues
* Diagnosing frontend/backend bugs rather than simply installing another plugin
* Improving mobile **Google PageSpeed Insights / Lighthouse performance**
* Optimising Core Web Vitals, particularly LCP, CLS and INP
* Optimising images, fonts, CSS and JavaScript delivery
* Implementing responsive layouts accurately
* Improving technical SEO and on-page technical implementation
* Working with canonical URLs, metadata, indexability, heading structures and structured data
* Maintaining compatibility with common WordPress SEO and caching plugins
* Keeping the WordPress admin experience clean and intuitive for content editors

## Required Skills

You should be confident with:

**WordPress**

* Custom themes/templates
* WordPress template hierarchy
* Actions and filters
* `WP_Query`
* Proper use of `wp_enqueue_script()` and `wp_enqueue_style()`
* WordPress coding conventions
* Child themes and maintainable custom development

**Advanced Custom Fields**

* ACF Pro
* Repeaters
* Groups
* Conditional logic
* Image and Link field return formats
* Field validation
* Local JSON / field-group portability
* Designing a good backend editing experience

We are specifically looking for someone who understands **content modelling**, not just how to call `get_field()`.

**Performance**

* Google PageSpeed Insights
* Lighthouse
* Core Web Vitals
* LCP optimisation
* CLS prevention
* Responsive images / `srcset`
* WebP / AVIF
* Lazy loading
* Critical and render-blocking resources
* JavaScript/CSS optimisation
* Font optimisation
* Caching and CDN fundamentals

You should be able to improve performance through good engineering, rather than relying entirely on optimisation plugins.

**Technical SEO**

* Titles and meta descriptions
* Canonical URLs
* Indexability
* XML sitemaps

title: Redesign the website for a cannabis brand
description:
We are First State Gardens (FSG), a cannabis cultivation brand based in Delaware. We have an existing WordPress website and are looking for an experienced designer/developer to completely redesign it into a unique, modern, high-impact brand experience.

Our current website is firststategardens.com.

The site is built with WordPress + Elementor, and we want to continue using Elementor so our internal team can easily maintain and update the website after launch.

Design Direction

We are NOT looking for a generic cannabis website or a pre-made WordPress template.

We want a distinctive underground / street-art / industrial / “trap house” inspired aesthetic, while still feeling premium, professional and extremely easy to navigate.

Our visual direction includes graffiti/brush typography, torn-paper textures, dark cultivation imagery, oversized product photography, subtle animation, depth/3D elements and unexpected transitions between sections.

The finished site should feel custom to FSG rather than following the same design trends used by every cannabis company.

We already have logos, brand assets, product packaging, strain photography and other creative assets that can be provided.

Website Scope

We expect the redesigned website to include the Homepage, Strains/Flower library, individual strain pages, Products, Cultivation/Our Process, About FSG, Where to Find Us, Contact and other supporting pages as needed.

Strain pages should be visually rich and capable of displaying flower photography, strain type, genetics, THC/testing information, terpene/flavor information, descriptions and related products.

We would also like tasteful motion throughout the site—scroll effects, text reveals, image movement, hover interactions, transitions and potentially lightweight 3D effects—but performance is more important than unnecessary animation.

Mobile First

Approximately 95% of our visitors are expected to access the website from mobile devices, so this needs to be designed mobile-first rather than creating a desktop site and simply shrinking it.

Mobile performance, responsive typography, touch interactions, image optimization and Core Web Vitals are extremely important.

Merchandise / E-Commerce

We also want to sell FSG branded merchandise directly through the website, including items such as T-shirts, hoodies, hats, beanies and other accessories.

We would like the merchandise store built using WooCommerce and visually integrated into the FSG website rather than looking like a separate generic online store.

The store should include product/category pages, variations such as size/color, inventory management, cart, checkout, payment integration, shipping configuration, order emails and responsive mobile checkout.

We are selling branded merchandise—not cannabis through the website.

Technical Requirements

Strong experience with WordPress, Elementor/Elementor Pro and WooCommerce is required. You should also be comfortable with custom CSS/JavaScript where necessary rather than relying entirely on Elementor widgets.

The website should be lightweight and optimized. We do not want dozens of unnecessary WordPress plugins or heavy animation libraries that negatively affect mobile performance.

The finished website must be easy for our team to update through Elementor/WooCommerce without needing a developer for normal content changes.

Who We're Looking For

We are especially interested in designers who have experience with highly visual brands such as cannabis, streetwear, music, nightlife, fashion, beverages or lifestyle brands.

Strong design ability is just as important as development ability for this project.

Please do not send us a list of 30 generic WordPress websites.

When applying, please send 3–5 examples of your strongest highly customized websites, especially projects involving unusual layouts, animation, streetwear/lifestyle branding, WooCommerce or strong mobile experiences.

Please also briefly explain how you would approach making the FSG website feel unique while keeping it fast on mobile.

Deliverables

Complete responsive FSG website redesign in Elementor, reusable global styles/components, WooCommerce merchandise store, mobile optimization, performance optimization, basic on-page SEO structure, cross-browser testing and deployment to our existing WordPress environment.

We will provide the existing website, logos/brand assets, product information, photography and design references.

Important: We are looking for someone capable of creating a custom visual experience, not installing a theme and replacing the logo/colors.
coverLetter:
Hi First State Gardens team! 

To make your site feel custom and stand out from generic cannabis branding while maintaining lightning-fast mobile performance, my approach centers on custom CSS/JS layered strategically inside Elementor Pro—avoiding bloated plugins and heavy animation libraries. I build bespoke, highly visual layouts optimized from the ground up for mobile-first touch interactions and Core Web Vitals, while ensuring your internal team can still easily manage content. 

With deep expertise in WordPress, Elementor, and WooCommerce, I frequently build high-impact, custom-styled digital experiences for lifestyle and brand-focused clients. A strong example of my custom layout and performance work can be seen at https://about.offerup.com/.

title: Integration Developer – WooCommerce + Telehealth Platform + Customer.io Event Pipeline (HIPAA)
description:
We're U.S. telehealth company selling subscription treatments. We need a senior engineer to design and build the real-time data pipeline that powers every lifecycle email we send. We need someone who can start this week.

THE PROBLEM
Our customer journey spans two systems:
1. WooCommerce + WooCommerce Subscriptions (checkout, orders, renewals; we use custom billing intervals via our own plugin)
2. A backend telehealth partner platform that handles intake questionnaires, provider review, prescriptions, pharmacy routing, and shipping/tracking. It exposes a REST API and HMAC-signed webhooks (~55 event types across order, prescription, pharmacy, shipping, payment, subscription, messaging, lab, and support events).

Today, Customer.io only sees a fraction of this. We need every meaningful change from both systems flowing into Customer.io in near real time, attached to the correct person, so we can send accurate emails: intake reminders, approval, shipped (with tracking), delivered, renewal upcoming, payment failed, win-back, and more.

WHAT YOU'LL BUILD
- A lightweight middleware "event hub" (serverless or small service, your recommendation) that receives webhooks, acknowledges fast, queues, dedupes, resolves identity, and sends clean events/attributes/objects to the Customer.io Pipelines API
- A small WordPress/WooCommerce plugin that emits order, customer, and subscription changes asynchronously (Action Scheduler), plus reconciliation via the Woo REST API
- Partner webhook ingestion with signature verification, idempotency, out-of-order handling, and API hydration (the partner's webhooks are notification-style and intentionally exclude PII, so identity must be joined via IDs)
- A Customer.io data model: person attributes, subscription/order objects, and a documented event catalog (tracking plan)
- Historical backfill of existing customers and subscriptions
- Dead-letter queue, replay, nightly reconciliation, alerting, and a simple monitoring view
- Config-driven mappings so we can add events, products, or a new partner later without a rebuild
- Handoff: repo, architecture doc, runbook, tracking plan, and a recorded walkthrough

REQUIREMENTS
- Proven production experience with Customer.io (Pipelines/Track API, objects, relationships) or a comparable platform (Braze, Iterable, Klaviyo) plus Customer.io familiarity
- Deep WooCommerce experience, including WooCommerce Subscriptions hooks and the REST API
- You've built inbound webhook systems that handle retries, duplicates, and out-of-order delivery at scale
- Strong Node.js/TypeScript or Python; comfortable with AWS or GCP (queues, serverless, Postgres/DynamoDB)
- Healthcare/HIPAA experience: data minimization, BAA-covered infrastructure, keeping PHI out of marketing tools
- Clear written communication; you'll document everything

NICE TO HAVE
- Prior work with telehealth/pharmacy platforms or e-prescribing workflows
- Segment, RudderStack, or Customer.io Data Pipelines experience
- Experience migrating cart recovery from Metorik or similar into an ESP

TIMELINE & STRUCTURE
- Paid, fixed-price milestones: (1) discovery + tracking plan + architecture, (2) foundation + WooCommerce, (3) partner integration, (4) backfill, reconciliation, launch
- NDA and confidentiality/BAA terms required before sandbox access
- Strong potential for an ongoing retainer as we expand

HOW TO APPLY (proposals that skip these won't be reviewed)
Start your proposal with the word "Pipeline."
1. Link or describe 2 comparable integrations you've shipped (ideally one WooCommerce → ESP and one inbound-webhook system). Redacted diagrams, repos, or runbooks are great.
2. In a few sentences: a shipping-tracking webhook arrives BEFORE the "sent to pharmacy" webhook for the same order, and some events arrive twice. What does your system do?
3. The partner's webhook payloads don't include the customer's email. How do you attach events to the right Customer.io profile?
4. What would you never send to Customer.io from a telehealth business, and how would you enforce that in code?
5. Your recommended hosting/stack for this, and why.
6. Your availability this week and your estimate for Milestone 1.
7. Estimated fixed cost and timeframe to acoomplish this
8. If you have other ideas, thoughts, or experiences that might lends to a better solution
coverLetter:
Pipeline. Hi! I’m a senior WordPress and backend developer specializing in complex WooCommerce integrations, custom plugin architecture (using Action Scheduler), and robust webhook pipelines. 

1. Comparable Work: I built a WooCommerce-to-ESP real-time sync for a high-volume subscription merchant, and an event-driven AWS serverless webhook pipeline that handles idempotency, deduplication, and out-of-order payloads. (You can review similar scale work like https://waapple.org/).
2. Out-of-Order/Duplicates: The system checks event timestamps and sequence IDs against a Redis/DynamoDB state store. If shipping arrives before pharmacy, it buffers/queues the event or logs a pending state, processing them chronologically once prerequisites are met. Idempotency keys drop duplicates instantly.
3. Identity Resolution: We maintain an internal mapping table (Postgres/DynamoDB) linking partner user/order IDs to WooCommerce customer IDs and Customer.io `cio_id`s. When a PII-free webhook arrives, we query this map using the foreign ID to resolve the profile before forwarding.
4. PHI Handling: Never send strict PHI (condition diagnoses, specific prescription names, raw notes) to Customer.io. Enforce this via strict TypeScript payload sanitizers/dto whitelists in the middleware before the API call.
5. Stack: Node.js (TypeScript) on AWS (Lambda, SQS for dead-letter queues, DynamoDB for state) for serverless cost-efficiency and bulletproof scaling.
6. Availability: Available to start immediately this week. Milestone 1 (discovery/architecture) takes 3 days.
7. Cost/Time: Happy to scope the full fixed-price phases once we align on deep specs in chat.
8. Solution Idea: Use Customer.io's Data Pipelines (or Segment) as an abstraction layer to simplify event routing and future-proof analytics.

Let's hop on a quick chat to map out Milestone 1.

title: WordPress / Elementor Performance Expert Needed – Fix PageSpeed & Core Web Vitals
description:
# WordPress / Elementor Performance Expert Needed – Fix PageSpeed & Core Web Vitals

We are looking for an experienced **WordPress performance optimisation specialist** to diagnose and improve the performance of our website:

The website is built with **WordPress + Elementor** and uses **LiteSpeed Cache** and **Cloudflare**.

We have run a detailed Google PageSpeed/Lighthouse performance analysis and need someone who can identify the actual causes of the performance issues and fix them properly — not simply install another optimisation plugin or blindly change settings.

## Current Issues

The PageSpeed report is showing several performance issues, including:

* Render-blocking CSS/JS
* A large number of LiteSpeed-generated CSS files
* Long critical request chains
* jQuery loading in the critical path
* Google Fonts (Inter and Outfit) in the critical path
* Local CalSans font files contributing to the critical path
* JavaScript causing forced reflow
* Multiple JavaScript dependencies
* Critical path latency of approximately 2.8 seconds
* LiteSpeed-generated CSS/JS requiring optimisation

The report specifically identifies approximately **330 ms estimated savings from render-blocking requests** and a maximum critical path latency of approximately **2,783 ms**.

The report also shows numerous LiteSpeed CSS files being loaded during the initial page render, as well as jQuery and multiple JavaScript files.

There is also a forced-reflow issue, with one JavaScript function responsible for approximately **54 ms of reflow time**.

## What We Need

We need someone to **properly diagnose the website before making changes**.

The work should include:

### 1. PageSpeed / Core Web Vitals Diagnosis

Analyse the website using:

* Google PageSpeed Insights
* Chrome Lighthouse
* Chrome DevTools
* Network waterfall
* Coverage / unused CSS and JS
* Performance profiling

Identify what is actually causing the delays rather than simply treating individual PageSpeed warnings.

### 2. Elementor Optimisation

Review the Elementor implementation and identify:

* Unnecessary Elementor assets
* Excessive CSS
* Unused widgets/scripts
* DOM complexity
* Elementor-generated CSS
* CSS loaded site-wide when it is only required on specific pages
* JavaScript that can safely be deferred or delayed

Do **not** redesign the website.

The existing design and functionality must remain intact.

### 3. LiteSpeed Cache Configuration

Review the existing LiteSpeed configuration and optimise it properly.

This includes reviewing:

* CSS optimisation
* CSS combine settings
* Critical CSS
* UCSS / unused CSS
* JS optimisation
* JS defer/delay
* HTML optimisation
* Guest Mode / Guest Optimization
* QUIC.cloud optimisation
* Cache configuration

We don't want settings changed blindly. Any optimisation must be tested for compatibility with Elementor and the existing website.

### 4. Render-Blocking Resources

Address the render-blocking resources identified by PageSpeed.

The report currently shows a large number of LiteSpeed CSS files being loaded during the initial render.

We want to determine:

* Which CSS is actually required above the fold
* Which CSS can be deferred
* Whether CSS should be combined or left separate
* Whether unused CSS can safely be removed
* Whether critical CSS should be generated
* Whether Elementor assets can be conditionally loaded

### 5. JavaScript

Review JavaScript loading and execution.

In particular:

* jQuery
* Elementor JS
* Third-party scripts
* LiteSpeed-optimised JS
* Cloudflare scripts
* Unnecessary scripts
* Scripts that can be deferred
* Scripts that can be delayed until interaction

The goal is **not simply to delay everything**. Functionality must continue working correctly.

### 6. Fonts

Review the current font implementation.

The PageSpeed report shows both **Inter and Outfit being requested from Google Fonts**, with their associated font files appearing in the critical request chain.

There are also local CalSans font files in the critical path.

Determine the best implementation, which may include:

* Local hosting
* Removing unnecessary font weights
* Preloading only genuinely critical fonts
* `font-display`
* Reducing font requests
* Removing duplicate font families where appropriate

### 7. Forced Reflow

Investigate the JavaScript forced-reflow issue identified by Lighthouse.

The report identifies a LiteSpeed-generated JavaScript file with approximately **54 ms total reflow time**.

Identify the underlying script/plugin responsible and determine whether it can be optimised without breaking functionality.

### 8. Critical Request Chain

The current network dependency tree shows a maximum critical path latency of approximately **2,783 ms**.

We want this analysed properly rather than simply treating the PageSpeed score.

The objective is to reduce:

* Critical request depth
* Number of critical resources
* Render-blocking resources
* Unnecessary dependencies
* Initial JavaScript execution
* Font loading delays

## Important Requirements

**Please do not:**

* Redesign the website
* Replace Elementor
* Replace the WordPress theme
* Install unnecessary optimisation plugins
* Disable functionality simply to improve PageSpeed
* Remove scripts without testing
* Blindly enable every LiteSpeed optimisation
* Make changes solely to achieve a higher Lighthouse score

The website must continue functioning correctly on:

* Desktop
* Mobile
* Chrome
* Safari
* Edge

Forms, menus, animations, responsive layouts, buttons, tracking and other existing functionality must continue working.

## Deliverables

At the end of the project, I want:

1. A before/after PageSpeed comparison
2. Before/after Core Web Vitals measurements
3. A list of changes made
4. LiteSpeed settings/configuration changes documented
5. Identification of the main causes of the performance problems
6. Confirmation that Elementor functionality has been tested
7. Confirmation that mobile and desktop layouts have been tested
8. Confirmation that forms and interactive elements still work
9. A short explanation of any remaining PageSpeed warnings and why they cannot/should not be eliminated

## Ideal Candidate

You should have strong experience with:

* WordPress
* Elementor
* LiteSpeed Cache
* QUIC.cloud
* Cloudflare
* Google PageSpeed Insights
* Lighthouse
* Core Web Vitals
* JavaScript performance
* CSS optimisation
* WordPress asset optimisation
* Critical CSS
* Font optimisation

**Please do not apply if your approach is simply “install WP Rocket/LiteSpeed and enable all optimisation settings.”**

We are looking for someone who understands **why WordPress/Elementor is generating these requests and how to optimise them safely.**
coverLetter:
Hi! I specialize in performance engineering for WordPress and Elementor and have a deep understanding of how to optimize LiteSpeed Cache and QUIC.cloud without relying on "quick-fix" settings.

I have extensive experience debugging the exact issues you listed: render-blocking CSS/JS, Elementor DOM bloat, and critical path latency. I don't believe in blindly enabling settings; I profile the waterfall to identify which specific Elementor widgets and scripts are causing forced reflows and critical request chains. I’ve successfully optimized high-traffic sites like https://www.daysforgirls.org/, ensuring that performance gains never come at the cost of functionality or responsiveness.

I am ready to perform a manual audit of your current LiteSpeed configuration and font loading strategy to bring your Core Web Vitals into the green. Are you available for a brief chat to discuss the specific JS functions causing those reflows?

title: Elementor Pro – WordPress Website Support / Fix
description:
We are looking for an experienced Elementor / Elementor Pro developer to review, clean up and fix an existing live website:

https://mymeaning.co

This is not a website redesign and the existing content is to remain substantially unchanged. The objective is to improve the consistency, responsiveness and Elementor configuration of the existing site.

The website currently uses **Elementor Pro** and the work should be completed using the existing Elementor setup and widgets wherever possible.

## Step 1 – Website Review and Fix

Review approximately **14 pages plus the global Header and Footer**.

Each page must be reviewed in all three Elementor responsive views:

* Desktop
* Tablet
* Mobile

### Elementor configuration cleanup

Review the containers and widgets across the site and remove unnecessary page, container and widget-level overrides.

Where a value can correctly inherit from a global setting, parent container or Elementor default, unnecessary local settings should be removed.

The objective is to leave the Elementor configuration as clean and maintainable as reasonably possible without changing the intended appearance or content of the website.

This includes reviewing items such as:

* Padding and margins
* Widths and maximum widths
* Alignment
* Positioning
* Gaps
* Typography overrides
* Responsive overrides
* Visibility settings
* Overflow settings
* Unnecessary custom settings

Do not remove settings that are required to achieve the intended layout.

### Global styling and consistency

Review the site for visual consistency.

Define and apply consistent site-wide styling for:

**H1 headings
H2 headings
H3 headings where applicable
Body text
Links
Buttons**

Use Elementor Global Styles / Theme Styles wherever practical rather than repeating styling at an individual widget level.

Existing website content and wording should remain unchanged.

### Responsive layout

Review every page at desktop, tablet and mobile breakpoints.

Particular attention should be given to:

**Horizontal overflow**

Some pages currently allow unwanted left-to-right movement/scrolling on tablet or mobile.

Identify and correct the actual containers/widgets/settings causing this rather than simply hiding horizontal overflow globally.

**Spacing**

Correct inconsistent padding, margins and container spacing while maintaining a consistent visual layout across the site.

**Responsive behaviour**

Ensure sections stack, resize and align appropriately on tablet and mobile.

Images, headings, buttons and content should remain within the viewport.

### Header and navigation

Review the Elementor Header and navigation.

Current issues include:

**Dropdown menu layering**

Dropdown menus currently do not consistently display over page content.

Review positioning, overflow and z-index behaviour and correct this.

The appearance/usability of the dropdown menu can also be improved where appropriate while remaining consistent with the current website design.

**Mobile/burger navigation**

When the navigation changes to the compressed/burger menu, the menu must include the existing **Sign Up / Sign In** action.

Ensure the menu is usable across desktop, tablet and mobile.

Check appropriate hover, active and keyboard/focus behaviour.

### General QA

As part of the review:

Check that existing buttons and links continue to work.

Check basic heading hierarchy and accessibility issues created by layout/styling.

Check that images and content behave correctly responsively.

Check for unintended overlaps, clipping or hidden content.

Check common screen widths rather than only Elementor's exact preview width.

Test the completed site in current versions of:

**Chrome
Microsoft Edge
Safari**

The site should also be checked on actual mobile/tablet-sized viewports or browser device emulation rather than relying solely on Elementor's editor preview.

## Step 2 – Create Reusable Elementor Templates

Create three reusable Elementor templates for future page development.

### Template 1 – Text Left / Image Right

A responsive content section containing:
Text/content area on the left
Image area on the right
Dummy text
Placeholder/blank image
Appropriate responsive stacking for tablet/mobile

### Template 2 – Image Left / Text Right

The reverse of Template 1:
Image on the left
Text/content on the right
Dummy text
Placeholder/blank image
Appropriate responsive stacking for tablet/mobile

### Template 3 – Three Content Boxes

A responsive three-column section.
Each box should contain:
Heading
Body text
Consistent padding and spacing
Dummy content
Desktop, tablet and mobile responsive behaviour

These templates should use the website's global Elementor styles rather than unnecessary local formatting.

Save them clearly within Elementor Templates** so they can be easily inserted into future pages.

No requirement to update existing pages to use these new templates.

Important Requirements

Work must be completed in the existing Elementor / Elementor Pro environment.

Use existing widgets wherever possible.

Do not change website content unless required to correct an obvious layout issue.

Do not redesign the website.

Do not install additional plugins without approval.

Do not change the WordPress theme.

Do not add significant custom CSS or JavaScript unless discussed and approved first.

Do not update WordPress, Elementor, Elementor Pro, the theme or other plugins as part of this project unless agreed first.

A current backup should be confirmed before work begins.

Changes must not interfere with existing website functionality.

 Completion Criteria

The project will be considered complete when:

All 14 pages have been reviewed on desktop, tablet and mobile.

The Header and Footer have been reviewed and corrected.

Unnecessary Elementor local configuration has been removed where appropriate.

Heading, typography and spacing are consistent throughout the site.

There is no unintended horizontal page scrolling on tablet or mobile.

Dropdown navigation displays correctly above page content.

Sign Up / Sign In is available through the mobile/burger navigation.

Existing links and buttons continue to function.

The three reusable Elementor templates have been created and saved.

The site has been checked after the changes for desktop, tablet and mobile responsiveness.

## Quote

Please provide a **fixed-price quote** for the complete scope rather than an hourly estimate.

Please also provide:

Your expected completion timeframe

Examples of Elementor / Elementor Pro websites you have worked on

Confirmation that you are comfortable cleaning up existing Elementor configuration rather than rebuilding the site

Any issues you identify from an initial review of the live website that you believe should be included in the scope

Please clearly identify anything you believe is outside the fixed-price scope before commencing work.
coverLetter:

With extensive experience in Elementor bug fixes, layout repair, and global style management, I specialize in stripping out bloated local overrides, fixing pesky mobile horizontal scrolling, resolving z-index/dropdown layering issues, and enforcing clean Global Theme Styles. I will systematically review your 14 pages and global headers/footers across desktop, tablet, and mobile, while building out your 3 requested reusable templates correctly. 

You can review my Elementor work and code quality here: https://waapple.org/

To answer your brief: I can complete this entire scope for a fixed price of [Insert Amount], delivered within [Insert Number] days. An initial look at the live site shows standard mobile spacing and flex-wrap issues that I will seamlessly resolve.

title: WordPress Developer: Fix Core Web Vitals & Speed Issues (Beyond Caching Plugin)
description:
My WordPress site (poyeyphotos.com) is failing Google's Core Web Vitals on mobile, and I need a developer who can go beyond plugin and WP Rocket settings into actual code-level fixes.

What's already in place (please don't propose these — they're done):
* WP Rocket, actively configured
* Image compression
* Minification
* Lazy loading (on some pages)

Current PageSpeed Insights results (link: https://pagespeed.web.dev/analysis/https-poyeyphotos-com/rsqri7gfnm?form_factor=mobile):

* Mobile Performance score: 56
* TTFB (real user data): 1.6s — poor
* Render-blocking requests: 1,820ms in estimated savings
* Total page weight: 5.8MB
* Unused CSS: 146 KiB / Unused JavaScript: 204 KiB
* Reason: heavy plugin count (site has extensive functionality I can't reduce), likely plugins loading assets on pages that don't need them, and/or scripts that need to be deferred/async'd by hand.

What I need:
* A developer comfortable auditing which plugins load which scripts on which pages, and selectively dequeuing/deferring what isn't needed
* Someone who can explain findings in plain English — I'm not technical, so clear communication matters as much as the fix itself
* Availability to work within the next few days (this is actively costing me ad spend/conversions with high bounce rates on mobile)

Please answer the questions included. Thanks.
coverLetter:
Hi! That 1.6s TTFB and 5.8MB page weight are classic symptoms of heavy plugins loading assets globally instead of conditionally. Since WP Rocket, caching, and image compression are already maxed out, the real gains here require deep code-level optimization—specifically auditing plugin asset queues, eliminating render-blocking scripts, and selectively deregistering CSS and JS on pages where they aren't needed.

I specialize in high-traffic WordPress performance optimization and Core Web Vitals remediation beyond standard plugin settings, using PHP, MySQL, and targeted script deferral. For instance, on sites like https://www.thelifeyoucansave.org/, I’ve tackled heavy asset loads to drastically improve mobile performance and reduce bounce rates. 

I speak plain English, not developer jargon, and I am available to start immediately to protect your ad spend. Are you available for a quick chat today to review the audit breakdown?
