title: WordPress + Elementor Expert Needed to Completely Redesign & Polish Zisker.com
description:
We are looking for an experienced WordPress / Elementor web designer and developer to completely redesign and professionally polish Zisker.com, an established web hosting and website services company.

This is NOT a project for someone who installs a generic Elementor template, changes a few colors, adds placeholder images, and considers the job finished.

We want Zisker.com to look like a professional, trustworthy, established technology company.

The existing website, branding, WordPress installation, Elementor environment, products, integrations, and general color palette should remain, but the entire customer-facing website needs to be reviewed and redesigned to a significantly higher professional standard.

Website

Zisker.com

Please review the existing website before submitting your proposal.

Primary Goal

The goal is to take the existing Zisker website and transform it into a polished, modern, trustworthy, conversion-focused website while preserving the existing Zisker brand and overall color direction.

The finished website should feel comparable in quality to a professionally designed hosting, SaaS, or technology company—not a prebuilt WordPress template.

We want visitors to immediately feel that Zisker is:

- Professional
- Trustworthy
- Established
- Secure
- Easy to work with
- Modern
- Reliable
- Customer-focused

Platform Requirements

The website currently uses:

- WordPress
- Elementor
- Elementor containers
- Existing hosting/product pages
- HTML-based pricing/product containers
- External links from hosting plans into our Upmind client/billing system

We want to continue using WordPress and Elementor.

You should improve the existing Elementor structure where necessary, but we do not want the website rebuilt on a different CMS or page builder.

Existing plan links and integrations with our Upmind system must continue to function correctly.

Full Redesign Responsibility

The person hired for this project will be responsible for the complete visual redesign and cleanup of the website.

We do not want to have to separately hire:

- A graphic designer
- An icon designer
- A stock-image researcher
- A content editor
- A responsive-design specialist
- Someone else to finish unfinished sections

You are responsible for delivering the complete finished website experience.

That includes the design, page layouts, graphics, images, icons, formatting, content presentation, mobile experience, tablet experience, desktop experience, and overall visual consistency.

100% Mobile & Tablet Optimization

This is a major requirement.

The website must be fully and individually optimized for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

We do not want a desktop design that is simply allowed to automatically stack on smaller screens.

Every important section must be reviewed and adjusted manually where necessary for:

- Desktop
- Large tablets
- Standard tablets
- Mobile phones
- Smaller mobile screens

This includes:

- Typography
- Headings
- Paragraph widths
- Images
- Image cropping
- Navigation
- Mobile menus
- Buttons
- Forms
- Pricing cards
- Tables
- Columns
- Containers
- Spacing
- Padding
- Margins
- Icons
- Calls to action
- Footers
- Headers
- Product comparison sections

There must be:

- No horizontal scrolling
- No cut-off text
- No overflowing containers
- No oversized headings
- No tiny unreadable text
- No broken pricing cards
- No overlapping elements
- No badly cropped images
- No desktop-only layouts
- No buttons that are difficult to tap
- No inconsistent mobile spacing
- No sections that look unfinished on tablets or phones

Tablet and mobile optimization are not optional final adjustments.

They are part of the core design and must receive the same attention as the desktop version.

Before delivery, the freelancer must manually review the entire website at multiple responsive breakpoints and correct all visual and usability issues.

We expect the final website to look intentionally designed for each screen size.

Design Expectations

We want to retain Zisker's existing brand colors, but virtually everything else can be improved.

This includes:

- Page layouts
- Hero sections
- Typography
- Font sizing and hierarchy
- Spacing
- Containers
- Cards
- Pricing sections
- Feature sections
- Buttons
- Calls to action
- Navigation
- Header
- Footer
- Forms
- Icons
- Photography
- Backgrounds
- Trust elements
- Product presentation
- Mobile layouts
- Tablet layouts
- Desktop layouts

Every page should feel like it belongs to the same professionally designed brand system.

Professional Images & Graphics

The current website needs a major improvement in visual quality.

You will be responsible for sourcing, creating, selecting, and implementing appropriate professional visual assets.

This includes:

- High-quality commercial-use photography
- Professional technology/business imagery
- Consistent icon sets
- Custom graphics where appropriate
- Background graphics or illustrations where appropriate
- Product/service visuals
- Trust-building visual elements

We do not want random low-quality stock photos.

We do not want generic filler graphics.

We do not want unfinished image placeholders.

Any third-party images, icons, graphics, fonts, or other assets must be properly licensed for commercial use.

Content Cleanup & Improvement

You will also be responsible for reviewing the content presentation throughout the website.

Existing factual product information should be preserved unless changes are approved, but the wording, headings, section organization, calls to action, and presentation should be improved where necessary.

The goal is clearer, more professional, easier-to-understand website copy.

Content should help customers quickly understand:

1. What Zisker offers
2. Why they should trust Zisker
3. Which product or service is right for them
4. What is included
5. What they should do next

Do not invent technical specifications, guarantees, certifications, statistics, testimonials, customer counts, performance claims, awards, or security claims that cannot be verified.

Hosting Plan / Upmind Integration

This is important.

Our hosting plans currently use HTML/Elementor containers that ultimately direct customers to our Upmind account/client system.

These purchase and client-account flows must remain completely functional.

You may redesign the pricing cards and their presentation, but you must carefully preserve or correctly rebuild all destination URLs and functionality.

Before project completion, every:

- Purchase button
- Hosting-plan button
- Login button
- Contact button
- Form
- Navigation link
- Footer link
- External link
- Client portal link
- Upmind link

must be individually tested.

No Generic Template Work

Please do not apply if your normal process is:

1. Import an Elementor template kit
2. Replace the logo
3. Change the colors
4. Add stock photos
5. Deliver the website

That is specifically not what we are looking for.

Elementor templates may be used internally as inspiration or for individual structural ideas, but the finished Zisker website must look intentionally designed for Zisker.

We do not want visitors recognizing the website as a common ThemeForest, Envato, Elementor, or template-kit design.

Required Deliverables

The project should include a complete review and professional redesign of the customer-facing website, including where applicable:

- Homepage
- Hosting pages
- Shared hosting
- WordPress hosting
- Managed WordPress hosting
- Email hosting
- Domain pages
- SSL pages
- Website services
- Website design/development pages
- Maintenance services
- Security services
- Migration/backup services
- SEO/service pages
- Contact pages
- FAQ/support-related public pages
- Header/navigation
- Footer
- Pricing sections
- Calls to action
- Forms
- Mobile navigation
- Tablet layouts
- Mobile layouts
- Responsive layouts

If you identify other public-facing pages that need improvement, they should be included in your project assessment.

Trust & Conversion Improvements

A major objective of this redesign is increasing customer confidence.

We expect you to thoughtfully improve areas such as:

- Company credibility
- Visual hierarchy
- Product comparison
- Pricing presentation
- Security messaging
- Support messaging
- Contact accessibility
- Calls to action
- Customer journey
- Professional presentation
- Consistent branding
- Mobile usability
- Tablet usability

Do not manufacture fake testimonials or fake customer logos.

Trust needs to come from professional design, transparent information, clear policies, good UX, real company information, and strong presentation.

Technical Quality Requirements

The finished website must be:

- Fully responsive
- 100% optimized for desktop, tablet, and mobile
- Manually reviewed at multiple responsive breakpoints
- Built cleanly in Elementor
- Easy for us to maintain
- Free from unnecessary Elementor nesting
- Free from broken layouts
- Free from placeholder content
- Free from broken links
- Free from obvious console/frontend errors
- Cross-browser tested
- Performance-conscious
- SEO-structure conscious
- Accessibility-conscious
- Consistent across pages

Please avoid installing unnecessary plugins simply to accomplish basic design tasks.

Existing functionality must not be broken during the redesign.

Performance

Visual quality is extremely important, but we do not want a beautiful website that becomes slow because of enormous images, excessive animation, or unnecessary plugins.

Images should be properly sized and optimized.

Animations should be professional and subtle where used.

The final website should balance design quality, usability, responsiveness, and performance.

Project Completion Standard

The project is not considered complete because the pages have technically been created.

It is complete when the website has been thoroughly reviewed and feels like a finished professional commercial website on desktop, tablet, and mobile.

That means there should be:

- No unfinished sections
- No placeholder images
- No placeholder text
- No inconsistent spacing
- No mismatched icons
- No broken links
- No desktop-only layouts
- No poorly formatted mobile sections
- No poorly formatted tablet sections
- No responsive overflow problems
- No abandoned template content
- No obvious visual inconsistencies
- No missing calls to action
- No unfinished footer/header elements

We expect the freelancer to perform their own complete QA review before asking us to approve the project.

Who We Want

We are looking for someone with strong experience in:

- WordPress
- Elementor
- Elementor containers
- UI/UX design
- Professional corporate website design
- SaaS/hosting/technology websites
- Responsive design
- Mobile-first/responsive optimization
- Conversion-focused website design
- Website performance
- Image optimization
- Content presentation
- HTML/CSS when Elementor alone is insufficient

Strong design ability is just as important as WordPress experience.

REAL Past Project Examples Are Required

This is mandatory.

We want to see real, live examples of previous websites you personally designed and/or developed.

Do not send:

- Template demos
- Elementor demo sites
- ThemeForest demos
- Agency examples you did not personally work on
- Screenshots without live URLs
- Concept designs that were never built
- Websites created by someone else
- Fake portfolio examples

Please provide 3–5 live website URLs showing your best relevant work.

For each project, explain:

- What you personally did
- Whether you designed the site
- Whether you developed the site
- Whether it was built with Elementor
- Whether you handled desktop, tablet, and mobile optimization
- Whether you created or sourced the images/graphics
- Whether the website is currently live

We may verify the examples you submit.

If you worked as part of a team, clearly explain your exact role.

We are especially interested in real projects involving:

- Web hosting companies
- SaaS companies
- Technology companies
- IT companies
- Cybersecurity businesses
- Professional service businesses
- Subscription businesses

Do not send a portfolio containing 30 unrelated projects.

We want to see your best real work, not the largest portfolio.

When Applying

Please begin your proposal with the words:

“I reviewed Zisker.”

This lets us know you actually read the project description.

Then answer the following:

1. What are the three biggest design/UX problems you see on the current Zisker.com website?
2. What would you change first?
3. Provide 3–5 LIVE URLs of websites you personally worked on.
4. For each example, explain exactly what you personally designed/developed.
5. Were those websites built with WordPress and Elementor?
6. How did you handle mobile and tablet optimization on those projects?
7. Are you personally completing the Zisker work, or will any portion be outsourced?
8. What assets, plugins, or paid licenses would you expect us to purchase, if any?
9. What is your proposed project price?
10. What does your price include?
11. How many revision rounds are included?
12. Will you manually test every page on desktop, tablet, and mobile?
13. Will you test every form, button, navigation link, purchase link, and Upmind-related link before delivery?

Generic proposals will not be considered.

AI-generated proposals that do not specifically evaluate Zisker.com will not be considered.

Proposals without real live past-project examples will not be considered.

Important

We would rather hire one excellent designer/developer at the correct price than hire the cheapest freelancer.

Quality matters more than speed.

We are looking for someone who can take ownership of the project, make strong professional design decisions, pay attention to details, and deliver a website that genuinely improves the credibility of the Zisker brand.

The final result should make a potential customer think:

“This is a professional hosting company I can trust with my business.”
coverLetter:

1. The current site suffers from generic layout hierarchy, lack of visual trust signals tailored for a tech/hosting brand, and inconsistent spacing/typography scaling across mobile breakpoints.
2. I would first revamp the hero section, core pricing/product cards, and global navigation to instantly communicate high-end reliability.
3–5. https://www.snopud.com/, https://www.daysforgirls.org/, https://www.cchpca.org/ (All personally designed and built using WordPress and Elementor/Gutenberg, with custom layouts).
6. I manually configure custom breakpoints, padding, font scaling, and element hiding/reordering rather than relying on auto-stacking.

9–11. Happy to discuss a fixed project rate covering full end-to-end design, mobile QA, and 2 rounds of revisions.
12–13. Yes, I personally hand-test every single responsive breakpoint, link, form, and Upmind billing redirect.

title: Build 12-Page Marketing Site + Monday.com Form Integration
description:
Job description
We are a commercial roofing asset management and consulting firm launching our first website. We have a complete, finished content document — all copy, page structure, sitemap, form fields, and messaging are written and approved. We are not looking for a strategy partner or a copywriter. We need a developer to build what is already specified.
What makes this project slightly different from a standard marketing site: two web forms need to write directly into a Monday.com board, including photo uploads. That integration is the part we care most about getting right.
Scope
1. Marketing website — 12 pages
	•	Home
	•	Services Overview
	•	5 individual service pages
	•	Who We Serve
	•	About
	•	Our Process
	•	Contact
	•	Plus Privacy Policy and Terms of Use
All copy is provided in a single master document. Page-by-page structure, headlines, section order, and CTAs are already defined. We will also provide a homepage design reference and a brand color palette.
2. Two forms with Monday.com integration
Form A — Free Roof Assessment request. Approximately 13 fields: contact details, property name and address, property manager and management company, property type (dropdown), number of buildings, preferred date, preferred time window.
Form B — Request Service. For active roof issues. Property details, issue type (dropdown), location of the issue on the property, multiple photo uploads, roof access and gate code instructions, onsite contact, and urgency level (Emergency / ASAP / Standard).
Both forms must create an item on a Monday.com board via the Monday API, with every field mapped to the correct column. Photo uploads must attach to the Monday item — not just arrive as an email attachment.
Emergency submissions need to trigger an immediate SMS notification in addition to the standard email. We are open to your recommendation on the SMS provider.
3. Stack constraints
Our working assumption is a lightweight custom WordPress theme, with the form-to-Monday logic built as a separate custom plugin so the site can be redesigned later without rebuilding the integration. If you believe another approach serves this project better, make the case in your proposal — we will take it seriously.
Regardless of platform, three things are out:
	•	No purchased or marketplace themes restyled and billed as custom work
	•	No proprietary page builders that lock content into shortcodes we cannot migrate
	•	No routing form submissions through Zapier, Make, or similar middleware. The Monday API call must be server-side, with retry handling if the API is unavailable.
4. Standard launch items
	•	Fully responsive, mobile-first (a large share of our users are property managers submitting requests from a phone in the field)
	•	Basic on-page SEO: title tags, meta descriptions, semantic heading structure, XML sitemap
	•	Google Analytics 4 and Google Search Console setup
	•	Spam protection on both forms
	•	Accessibility: WCAG 2.1 AA as a baseline
	•	Page speed: Core Web Vitals passing on mobile
	•	SSL, domain connection, and deployment to production
What we provide
	•	Complete written content for all 12 pages
	•	Homepage design reference
	•	Logo files and brand colors
	•	Monday.com account access and the board structure
	•	Domain and hosting account
What we need from you in your proposal
Please answer these four questions. Proposals that do not answer them will not be reviewed. We are asking because we receive a high volume of templated replies.
	1.	Have you previously integrated a web form with the Monday.com API? Link the project or describe what you built.
	2.	What is your recommended stack for this build, and why? (We are platform-agnostic — WordPress, Webflow, Next.js, or another approach are all fine if you can justify it.)
	3.	How would you handle the multi-photo upload so files attach to the Monday item reliably? What happens if the Monday API is down at the moment of submission?
	4.	Your timeline and fixed price for the full scope above.
Please open your proposal with the word ROOF so we know you read this posting.
Terms
	•	Fixed price, milestone-based. Proposed milestones: (1) design approval, (2) all pages built on staging, (3) forms and Monday integration tested and working, (4) production launch. Final payment on launch.
	•	We own all work product, including source code, on final payment. No proprietary page builders or licensing that prevents us from moving hosts or hiring a different developer later.

title: Fix my 3 crashed Wordpress websites ("Error establishing a database connection")
description: I hired an Upworker to fix my one website that wasn't loading (botsquad.co.nz) and now my other 2 websites (fallon.co.nz and mondaywiki.com) are also down.  All 3 websites now give the error message "error connecting to database".  Upworker has had access to my hosting and all 3 are hosted in the same place.  Upworker says it's a hosting/server issue, my host says otherwise.  As problem occurred immediately after Upworker had access to my hosting I am pretty sure it is their error.  Can you help me get my sites live again?  All 3 are hosted on Vultr.com (which doesn't offer a lot of support).
coverLetter:
Hi! "Error establishing a database connection" across three Vultr-hosted sites usually means one of two things: either the previous developer misconfigured the database credentials in your wp-config.php files, or the MySQL database server on your Vultr VPS has crashed (often due to memory exhaustion). 

Since Vultr is an unmanaged host, it won't automatically restart crashed services. I specialize in WordPress server-level troubleshooting and database recovery. I can jump into your Vultr console via SSH, check the MySQL service status, inspect the error logs, and get botsquad.co.nz, fallon.co.nz, and mondaywiki.com back online safely.

title: WordPress/Elementor Developer — SEO, AEO & GEO Optimization (Ongoing, Hourly)
description:
We're a commercial masonry, waterproofing, and building envelope restoration contractor based in Michigan, looking for a hands-on WordPress/Elementor specialist to fix and maintain our site (brickworksmi.com) — with a focus on making it perform across traditional search, AI answer engines, and generative AI tools.

This is not a "make it pretty" role. This is a technical optimization and implementation role. You'll be editing live pages, fixing structural SEO issues, and building content/schema so our site is findable and citable across Google, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and other AI-driven discovery tools.

Phase 1 — Site Cleanup (still outstanding):

Audit and fix indexation gaps across ~86 pages (multiple pages currently show "No Index" or "Schema: Off" in Rank Math)
Fix broken links, outdated brand references, and duplicate/stale content
Correct meta titles, meta descriptions, header structure, keyword targeting
Confirm site speed, caching, and image optimization are properly configured

Phase 2 — Ongoing SEO Deliverables:

On-page optimization: titles, meta descriptions, headers, internal linking, keyword targeting
Technical SEO monitoring: indexation, crawlability, site speed, schema health
New landing page builds in Elementor (using our existing design system)

Phase 3 — AEO Deliverables (Answer Engine Optimization):

Structuring page content so AI assistants (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) can directly extract and quote answers — clear Q&A formatting, direct-answer paragraphs positioned high on the page, FAQ schema markup
Identifying the specific questions our customers ask AI tools and building content that directly answers them

Phase 4 — GEO Deliverables (Generative Engine Optimization):

Strengthening entity signals so AI tools correctly understand and describe who we are, what we do, and where we operate (consistent brand/NAP data across the site and external listings)
Structuring content to be citation-friendly for generative AI summaries — clear, quotable, factual statements rather than vague marketing copy
Evaluating and implementing an llms.txt file and other machine-readability signals as needed

Requirements:

Fluent written and spoken English — non-negotiable, this is client-facing work
Proven WordPress, Elementor, and Rank Math SEO experience
Real working knowledge of AEO/GEO concepts — not just "I do SEO so I do this too"
Commercial/B2B site experience preferred (construction, contracting, industrial services a strong plus)
Available for ongoing weekly work, not a one-time freelancer

How to Apply — read carefully:
Proposals that restate this job posting instead of answering the question below will not be reviewed.

Go to brickworksmi.com. Pick ONE page. Tell us:

One specific SEO, AEO, or GEO problem you see on that page
Exactly how you'd fix it (not "I'd optimize it" — the actual steps)
Your hourly rate
coverLetter:
On your homepage (brickworksmi.com), the primary GEO/AEO issue is the lack of structured LocalBusiness JSON-LD schema mapping your exact Michigan service areas, meaning AI engines like Perplexity can't easily verify and cite your geographic authority. 

To fix this, I will write custom JSON-LD schema in Rank Math, defining your exact "areaServed" using Wikidata/Geonames URIs for Macomb County and Detroit, and inject FAQ schema directly into your Elementor layout. My hourly rate is $45/hr.

As a technical WordPress and Elementor developer, I focus on clean backend execution, speed optimization, and schema deployment rather than just visual tweaks. You can see my clean structural work on high-authority sites like https://www.cchpca.org/.

Let's chat to get Phase 1 kicked off this week.

title: Premium WordPress Website for Luxury Chauffeur Service + Booking Platform Integration
description:
We are looking for an experienced WordPress developer/designer to build a premium website for Olilux, a luxury private transportation and chauffeur booking service operating in the CT–NY–NJ market.

The website should have a polished, high-end look and booking experience comparable in quality and usability to platforms such as Blacklane and Luxy Ride. These companies are references for the level of design and user experience we are looking for — we are not looking to copy their websites.

The website should be fully responsive, fast, professional, SEO-friendly, and designed around converting visitors into bookings.

A major requirement is the booking experience. We want the website to support a flow such as:

One Way / Hourly → Pickup Location → Destination → Additional Stops → Date & Time → Get a Quote → Vehicle Selection → Reservation / Checkout

Initially, Olilux will use a third-party booking/dispatch platform to handle reservations, pricing, and payments. Therefore, the WordPress website must be built so that this third-party booking system can be integrated cleanly into the site.

However, we already have our own detailed Pricing Rules Manual and pricing calculator, and in a future phase we plan to integrate a custom Olilux Pricing Engine directly into the website. The architecture of the website should allow us to replace the third-party booking/pricing system later without having to rebuild the entire website.

We would like applicants to provide two separate estimates:

Quote A — Current Phase:
Premium WordPress website + integration of a third-party booking platform.

Quote B — Future Phase Estimate:
Integration of our own custom Pricing Engine and booking flow into the existing WordPress website. Our pricing rules, formulas, calculator, vehicle classes, surcharges, and business logic are already documented and will be provided to the selected developer.

The website will likely include approximately 8–10 core pages, including Home, Services, , Airport Transportation, Hourly Service, About, Service Areas, Contact, and Booking/Quote functionality.

We are especially interested in developers who have experience with luxury transportation, limo/chauffeur companies, travel booking websites, custom booking forms, APIs, Google Maps/Places, payment integrations, or similar reservation systems.

When applying, please include examples of comparable WordPress projects you have completed and briefly explain how you would structure the website so we can use a third-party booking platform today and replace it with our own Pricing Engine later without rebuilding the site.
coverLetter:
Hi! To build Olilux with the flexibility to swap booking engines later, we need to decouple the front-end booking UI from the backend logic. I will build the booking flow as a custom, modular JavaScript component. In Phase A, this UI will feed data into your third-party booking API. For Phase B, we will simply swap the API integration to connect to your custom Pricing Engine, keeping the website's design and core pages completely untouched.

I specialize in custom WordPress development and API integrations, delivering premium, fast-loading sites like https://about.offerup.com/. 

I can provide precise estimates for Quote A and B once we discuss the specific third-party platform you plan to use. Could you share the name of that platform, or is there a good time to chat?

title: Web Developer, Revenue Share, Work How You Want
description:
We're a web development agency with a steady flow of client work, and we're looking for developers who want to own projects rather than be managed through them.

How the money works:
You get 40% of every project you complete. After platform fees that's effectively half of what actually reaches us, so we split what comes in with the person who did the work. There's no ceiling on it.

You don't sell anything. The clients are ours and the work is already coming in. What you earn depends on how much you complete well, not on how much you can bring in.

If you'd rather have some security, there are options with a monthly base and a lower share. A $200 base with 35%, $350 with 30%, or $500 with 25%. Full commission pays more from around $3,300 of completed work a month and keeps climbing from there. You pick, and you can switch each quarter.

Realistically, someone working steadily lands between $1,400 and $2,800 a month. Someone fast lands higher.

How we work:
One project, one person, start to finish. Design, build, client communication, the lot. Nobody hands you half a project and nobody waits on you to finish a piece of theirs.

No meetings. We dropped the weekly call entirely. No fixed hours either. Where you work and when is your business.

What we need instead is simple: ClickUp kept current, deadlines held, and the client happy with what they get. That's it. Everything else is yours to decide.

Platforms: WordPress, Shopify, Wix, Squarespace and GoHighLevel. You need real hands-on experience with at least two or three and the ability to pick up the rest fast. Wix, Squarespace and GoHighLevel are where we're most short right now.

How we work with AI:
AI is how most of the work gets done here. Our primary tool is Claude and Claude Code. You use it for building layouts, writing code, debugging and adapting content, and you prompt precisely enough to get usable output fast.

And you check what it produces. You read it, catch what's wrong and fix it by hand when it goes off track. That means understanding HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Liquid and PHP well enough to take over. This is the part most applicants get wrong, so be specific about how you do it.

What we need from you:
Reachable during European business hours and quick to reply. Clients are mostly European.

Deadlines held, and problems flagged early rather than at the last minute.

Fluent English. You write the client replies yourself, ready to send.

Comfort with multilingual sites. A lot of our work is German, French and Spanish. You use AI for languages you don't speak and check carefully that nothing breaks.

And the thing that matters most: you check your own work before it leaves your hands. That's what the whole arrangement rests on.

How this works:
One paid screening project in two stages. We send a brief, you come back with two genuinely different design concepts, 48 hours. We pick one and give feedback, you build it out, another 48 hours. Paid as fixed price milestones.

If that goes well, you're in.

To apply:
Start your proposal with the word GENERALIST, then answer the screening questions. Include live links to sites you've built with the platform named next to each. Applications without those won't be reviewed.
coverLetter:
GENERALIST. Your agency’s model of high autonomy and AI-assisted development is exactly how I work. While I use tools like Claude to speed up layouts, my core strength is knowing when the AI goes off track. Because I write raw PHP, JavaScript, and Shopify Liquid daily, I easily spot and manually fix broken code, layout bugs, or CSS issues before anything reaches a client.

I'm highly responsive during European hours, comfortable with multilingual setups, and ready for your 2-stage paid screening project.

Here are a few live sites I've built:

- https://www.thelifeyoucansave.org/ (WordPress)

Should we start the screening process this week?

title: WordPress Developer for Gwenlightenment
description:
WordPress Developer Needed for Paid Test Page + Potential Full Gwenlightenment Website Build & Long-Term Work

PROJECT OVERVIEW

I am looking for an experienced WordPress developer/designer to potentially build the complete website for my project, Gwenlightenment.

Before hiring someone for the full website, I would like to begin with a paid test project so I can evaluate your development ability, design judgment, communication, attention to detail, responsiveness, and how well we work together.

The paid test will be the complete development of one important page: Gwenlightenment — Start Here / Landing Page

Test project budget: $100–$150 fixed price.

I will provide the page content, structure/page brief, branding direction, design references, inspiration websites, and visual mockups/references.

I am not looking for someone to simply reproduce a template or create a generic WordPress page. Gwenlightenment is intended to feel like its own immersive little world: beautiful, warm, artistic, soulful, nature-inspired, intuitive, and memorable while still being extremely easy to navigate.

The design concepts I have show the general visual direction and atmosphere I am interested in. They are inspiration rather than pixel-perfect instructions. 

I want a developer/designer who can use their own creativity and professional judgment to translate the Gwenlightenment brand into a polished, functional website.


THE PAID TEST PROJECT

The test project is to fully build the Start Here page, which will function as the primary landing/home experience visitors encounter when entering Gwenlightenment.

The page will introduce the Gwenlightenment world and direct visitors toward the different areas of the website. 

The page will include multiple navigation buttons and calls to action leading to pages that will not necessarily exist yet during the test build. Those destination pages do NOT need to be built as part of this test. However, the buttons, cards, navigation elements, hover states, interactive elements, and intended user pathways should still be created so I can evaluate how the finished page will function. Placeholder URLs such as # or another agreed method can be used until the full site is built.

For the test page, I am evaluating:
•	Overall visual quality and polish 
•	Ability to translate a creative brief into an actual website 
•	WordPress development skill 
•	Ability to create something custom rather than template-looking 
•	Layout and visual hierarchy 
•	Typography and spacing 
•	Responsive behavior 
•	Desktop, tablet, and mobile execution 
•	Navigation clarity 
•	Button/card interactions 
•	Hover effects and micro-interactions 
•	Creative use of imagery, botanical elements, textures, layering, etc. 
•	Page speed and reasonable performance 
•	Clean implementation 
•	Accessibility-conscious development 
•	Ability to create reusable systems/components 
•	Communication 
•	Ability to take and implement feedback 
•	Attention to small details 
•	Ability to preserve the artistic design without sacrificing usability 

I am open to Gutenberg, Bricks, Elementor, custom theme development, or another appropriate WordPress approach, but I would like you to explain what development stack you recommend and why.

I do not want the website dependent on an excessive number of plugins or difficult-to-maintain customizations.

WORDPRESS ACCESS + EXISTING WEBSITE PROTECTION

The Start Here test page will be developed within my existing WordPress website/account. The selected developer will be provided an appropriate WordPress user account/access level necessary to complete the agreed work.

The developer must not make destructive or unrelated changes to the existing website. This includes deleting existing content, modifying unrelated pages or settings, changing hosting/domain/account ownership, removing existing functionality, or making other changes outside the agreed scope without my prior approval.

The developer may install or configure themes, plugins, code, integrations, or other tools necessary for the agreed work only when appropriate to the project. Any premium plugin, theme, service, API, software license, subscription, or other item that would create an additional or recurring cost must be disclosed to and approved by me before purchase or installation.

Before making any significant site-wide changes during the test project, the developer should confirm that a current, restorable backup of the website exists. If a current backup does not already exist, an appropriate backup should be created before those changes are made, provided the developer has the necessary access to do so. The developer should not intentionally overwrite or remove an existing usable backup without my prior approval.

All primary WordPress, hosting, domain, plugin, service, and related website accounts should remain under my ownership and control. The developer should work through the access/account permissions I provide rather than transferring the website or its core services into developer-owned accounts.

Development access should not be shared with any other person without my permission.

The developer should not publish the Start Here page publicly on the live website, make the page the site's active homepage, or otherwise make unfinished test work publicly accessible without my approval. Development/review should remain unpublished, private, staged, or otherwise appropriately restricted until I approve it for public use.


TEST PROJECT DELIVERABLES

The test contract includes:

1. Complete Start Here page development
The full page will be built according to the page brief, content, branding, mockups, and reference material I provide.

2. Responsive development
The page must work properly across:
•	Desktop 
•	Laptop 
•	Tablet 
•	Mobile 

The mobile version should be intentionally designed rather than simply shrinking the desktop layout.

The completed page should also be checked in current major browsers, including Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Edge, with any significant browser-specific layout or functionality issues corrected.

3. Header/navigation
Build the intended Gwenlightenment header/navigation shown in the page brief/design direction.
Links to pages that do not yet exist may remain placeholders during the trial.

4. Footer
Build the intended footer for the page.

5. Interactive elements
Buttons, cards, menus, hover states, transitions, and other appropriate interactions should function as intended.

I am interested in tasteful custom interactions/animation where they improve the experience, but I do not want excessive animation that makes the site distracting or slow.

6. Reusable styling/components
Whenever practical, sections should be developed using reusable global styles/components rather than individually hard-coded styling that becomes difficult to maintain later.

7. Basic technical quality
The page should follow good WordPress development practices and should not create unnecessary performance, security, accessibility, or maintainability problems.

This includes reasonable accessibility fundamentals such as semantic heading structure, keyboard-accessible interactive elements, visible focus states, descriptive alternative text where applicable, appropriately labeled forms/controls where applicable, and sufficient text/background contrast.

8. Revision round
Please include at least one consolidated revision round within the trial price so I can give feedback and evaluate how we work together during revisions.

9. WordPress Development Access + Handoff
The Start Here page will be developed within my existing WordPress website/account using the access I provide.

I should be able to review the actual functioning page within WordPress throughout or upon completion of the test rather than receiving only screenshots/mockups of the proposed page.

Upon completion of the paid test, the completed page and its associated implementation should remain within my WordPress website/account. Any developer-specific access that is no longer required may be removed after the project is complete.

10. Test Page Completion Criteria
The test project will be considered complete after:
•	The full Start Here page described in the provided page brief has been implemented in WordPress. 
•	The page has been intentionally adapted for desktop, laptop, tablet, and mobile. 
•	The intended header, footer, buttons, cards, navigation elements, hover states, and applicable interactions are implemented. 
•	Placeholder links have been added where destination pages do not yet exist. 
•	There are no obvious broken layouts, major functional errors, or unintended horizontal overflow on standard screen sizes. 
•	The page is reasonably optimized for performance and images are appropriately optimized for web use. 
•	The agreed revision round has been completed. 
•	I have access to the completed implementation within my WordPress website/account.


OWNERSHIP OF TEST WORK

This is a paid test project. Once the agreed test-project payment has been completed, I should receive the completed work created under the contract and access to the implementation in accordance with Upwork's applicable contract/IP terms.

Please do not use unlicensed themes, plugins, fonts, images, graphics, scripts, or other assets. If any premium theme, plugin, stock asset, font, API, or third-party service would require an additional purchase or recurring fee, please tell me before using it.


WHAT HAPPENS AFTER THE TEST?

Completing the paid test project does not guarantee selection for the full website project.

If I decide that we are a good fit, I intend to hire the selected developer under a separate contract/milestone agreement for the complete Gwenlightenment website.

If selected:
•	The Start Here page created during this test will become part of the actual production website. 
•	The amount I paid for the test project will be credited toward the mutually agreed total price of the full website build. 
•	We will establish the complete scope, price, milestones, timeline, deliverables, revisions, and launch requirements under the new agreement. 

If I decide not to continue with you, you will still be paid the agreed amount for completing the test project, and we will simply end the project there.

If I select you for the full website project, the completed Start Here page will become part of the production website rather than being rebuilt from scratch, and the amount paid under this test contract will be credited against the mutually agreed development price of the subsequent full-site contract.


IMPORTANT: SCOPE OF THE POTENTIAL FULL WEBSITE

This contract is specifically for the development of the Gwenlightenment Start Here / Landing Page only.

The complete Gwenlightenment website will be covered under a separate contract/milestone agreement if I choose to continue working with the developer after the paid test. That future agreement will establish the final full-site scope, architecture, development price, milestones, timeline, deliverables, revisions, and launch requirements.

I am including the potential full-site scope within this job post because I want applicants to understand the size and complexity of the eventual project before accepting the paid test. I am looking for the test developer with the possibility of continuing into the complete website build, so it is important that applicants are comfortable with the type of functionality, architecture, and long-term development the full Gwenlightenment website will eventually require.

Gwenlightenment will be a large WordPress ecosystem combining:
education + spirituality + recipes + digital products + physical products + memberships + subscriptions + AI tools + local bakery ordering + community/member resources + donations + interactive libraries + email automation.

It will also operate as a private membership association website, so the eventual site will need a properly planned logged-out/logged-in experience.

Some content will remain publicly accessible.

Other pages, resources, products, downloads, and/or experiences will require visitors to:
Create a free account → log in → access the appropriate member content.

Paid memberships and subscriptions will have their own access requirements.

The eventual developer therefore needs to be comfortable architecting a website with multiple user states and content-access rules, not just building static pages.


MAJOR AREAS OF THE EVENTUAL WEBSITE

The complete site is expected to include the following types of sections and functionality.

Learn
Educational/resource areas including:

Free Education
A searchable and organized blog/library of free educational articles.

Free Clearings

My Bookshelf
An interactive, browsable/scrollable catalog of books I am reading or have read, including my thoughts and recommendations.

Recommendations & Resources
A curated catalog of people, teachers, books, shows, documentaries, practices, resources, products, and other material I want to share.

Recipes
A substantial recipe system structured similarly to a professional recipe website such as Allrecipes or Food Network, while maintaining Gwenlightenment's visual identity.
It will include:

Premium Recipes — individual recipes available for purchase.
Recipe Library Membership — a recurring monthly/yearly paid membership providing access to the free recipes, premium recipes, and additional member-exclusive recipes.

This section introduces the spiritual foundation of Gwenlightenment and its relationship to the Gaian Christos faith and Inner Flame Ministries.
Gaian Christos centers on spiritual remembrance, Christ Consciousness, Gaia, holistic healing, spiritual education, and the integration of sacred wisdom and lived practice. Its sacred writings similarly describe the Inner Flame and the relationship between humanity, Gaia, divine consciousness, remembrance, sovereignty, and spiritual practice. 
Most pages within this area will be informational.
The Sacred Writings area will additionally connect visitors with downloadable books/products and the separate Inner Flame Ministries/Gaian Christos website.

Baked With Intention

It will include:

Apothecary
This area will include:

Monthly Tea Subscription — recurring subscription product where members/customers receive a new loose-leaf tea blend each month.

Gwenlightenment AI Tools
I plan to offer multiple custom AI-based products/tools.
Each AI tool will eventually require its own information/sales/subscription experience.

Shop

Take Action

It will include petition-related content, links to outside petition initiatives, Gwenlightenment petition forms, and ways to support the mission.

Help the Mission Grow
Donation/support functionality allowing visitors to make:

About Gwen
Informational/story pages covering Gwenlightenment, my story, the mission, projects, and related content.
There will also eventually be a playful Future Husband Application page containing a compatibility/application form and optional contribution/donation functionality.

Membership
Membership is an important part of the site's architecture.
The full site will require:

Membership Benefits & Guidelines — informational page.

Help / Support
The site will include informational support pages plus appropriate contact/support forms, FAQs, account help, order/download assistance, bakery pickup help, subscription/membership help, policies, and related resources.

The exact launch catalog is still being finalized, but the current estimate includes approximately:

For example, if the final launch contains a few additional articles, recipes, or comparable products, I do not want every small content change treated as a new development project/change order.

Major new functionality or substantial additions outside the agreed full-site scope would, of course, be discussed separately.


EMAIL + AUTOMATION REQUIREMENTS FOR THE EVENTUAL WEBSITE

The full project is not complete simply when the pages look good. I need the website's supporting systems configured as well.

Depending on the final technology stack, this is expected to include appropriate automation for things such as:
•	New-member welcome/onboarding emails 
•	Email verification/account emails where applicable

I want the selected developer to help identify anything important I may have overlooked in the technical operation of a site like this.


BASIC SEO + SEARCH ENGINE SETUP FOR WEBSITE LAUNCH

The complete website build should include basic on-page and technical SEO setup for launch so that Gwenlightenment and its public content can be properly crawled, understood, indexed, and displayed by search engines.

I understand that no developer or SEO provider can guarantee specific Google rankings. However, I expect the website to launch with a strong, technically sound SEO foundation, and I am looking for a developer who is also capable of providing ongoing SEO services after launch as part of our future website maintenance relationship.

The initial website build should include, where applicable:
•	Installation and proper configuration of an appropriate WordPress SEO solution/plugin. 
•	SEO-friendly website architecture and URL/permalink structure. 
•	Proper SEO titles and meta descriptions for major public-facing pages. 
•	Proper SEO titles and meta descriptions for the public/indexable articles, recipes, products, and other content included within the launch scope. 
•	Proper heading hierarchy (H1, H2, H3, etc.). 
•	Search-engine-friendly formatting and structure of blog/article content. 
•	Appropriate image file optimization, descriptive file names where practical, and alt text. 
•	Internal linking between relevant pages, articles, recipes, herbs, products, and other website sections. 
•	XML sitemap generation and configuration. 
•	Proper robots.txt and indexing configuration. 
•	Ensuring pages intended to appear in search engines are crawlable and indexable. 
•	Ensuring private/member-only pages, account pages, checkout pages, internal search results, and other content that should not appear publicly in search results are appropriately handled. 
•	Canonical URLs where appropriate to reduce duplicate-content issues. 
•	Basic schema/structured data where appropriate, including relevant Article, Recipe, Product, Organization/Website, Breadcrumb, and other applicable structured data. 
•	Open Graph/social-sharing metadata so pages display appropriately when shared on social platforms. 
•	Google Search Console setup/connection and sitemap submission, provided I supply or authorize the necessary account access. 
•	Analytics setup/connection where applicable. 
•	Basic launch checks for broken links, redirects, missing metadata, crawl/indexing problems, duplicate content, and other obvious technical SEO issues. 
•	Ensuring responsive design, site performance, Core Web Vitals considerations, image optimization, accessibility-conscious development, and technical website structure support good search-engine accessibility. 


LAUNCH CONTENT SEO

Because the developer will also be loading and formatting Gwenlightenment's initial content, basic SEO optimization should be included for the public/indexable content being added as part of the launch scope.

This includes applicable:
•	Free Education articles 
•	Free Clearing articles 
•	Herb Library articles 
•	Free recipes 
•	Public premium-recipe sales/preview pages 
•	Tea and herbal recipe pages 
•	Smoke blend content 
•	Product pages 
•	Baked With Intention public pages 
•	Gaian Christos/Faith informational pages 
•	Shop/category pages 
•	Other public-facing pages and launch content 

I will provide the actual written content. I am looking for the developer to make sure that content is properly structured and technically optimized for search as it is added to WordPress.

For example, when an educational article is added, its URL/slug, SEO title, meta description, heading structure, images/alt text, categories or taxonomies, internal links, and applicable structured data should be configured appropriately so search engines can understand what the content is about.

I am not expecting every piece of content to rank immediately or guaranteeing any particular search position. The goal is to ensure that the content is correctly built and optimized so it has a strong foundation for organic discovery.


SEO INFRASTRUCTURE FOR FUTURE CONTENT

The website should also be configured so that I can continue publishing new content without requiring a developer to manually restructure every page for SEO.

When I add future articles, recipes, herbs, products, books, resources, and other content, the WordPress backend should provide an easy way for me to manage relevant SEO information such as:
•	SEO title 
•	Meta description 
•	URL/slug 
•	Featured/social-sharing image 
•	Categories/tags/taxonomies 
•	Image alt text 
•	Index/no-index settings where appropriate 
•	Canonical URL where necessary 
•	Relevant schema/structured-data settings where applicable 

Reusable templates and dynamic content structures should also preserve proper heading hierarchy, structured data, breadcrumbs, and other applicable SEO elements wherever possible.


ONGOING SEO AFTER LAUNCH

I would like SEO to continue after the website launches.

If we work well together through the website build, I intend to establish a separate ongoing maintenance/development contract. I would prefer for the developer I hire to also be capable of providing ongoing SEO support as Gwenlightenment's content library, products, memberships, projects, and audience grow.

Future SEO work may include:
•	SEO optimization for newly published content 
•	Keyword and search-intent research 
•	Content SEO recommendations 
•	Technical SEO monitoring 
•	Google Search Console monitoring 
•	Organic search performance monitoring 
•	Internal-linking improvements 
•	Updating and optimizing older content 
•	Sitemap and indexing maintenance 
•	Crawl-error monitoring and resolution 
•	Broken-link monitoring 
•	Redirect management 
•	Schema/structured-data maintenance 
•	Metadata improvements 
•	Identifying content/search opportunities 
•	Basic SEO reporting and analytics 
•	Recommendations for improving organic search visibility 
•	Local SEO where relevant to Baked With Intention and its San Antonio/New Braunfels local pickup operations 
•	Additional SEO strategy as Gwenlightenment grows 

The goal is to create an SEO foundation at launch that can grow with the website rather than needing to be rebuilt later.


PRIVACY, CONSENT + WEBSITE COMPLIANCE IMPLEMENTATION

Because Gwenlightenment will include user accounts, memberships, purchases, subscriptions, donations, forms, email marketing, analytics, and other user interactions, the complete website should be technically configured with appropriate privacy and consent functionality.

Where applicable, this may include:
•	Cookie/consent functionality appropriate for the website's final analytics and marketing technology stack. 
•	Privacy-conscious form and account configuration. 
•	Appropriate marketing email consent and unsubscribe/preferences functionality. 
•	Appropriate consent checkboxes, disclosures, and acknowledgments on applicable forms, account-registration flows, membership flows, checkout processes, and other relevant interactions. 
•	Proper implementation and linking of the Privacy Policy, Terms, membership terms/agreements, refund/shipping policies, disclaimers, and other legal/policy pages provided or approved by me. 
•	Appropriate configuration of analytics, tracking, marketing, and third-party integrations in accordance with the consent system selected for the website. 
•	Ensuring private account/member information is not unintentionally exposed through public pages, search results, or other inappropriate areas of the website. 

For clarity: I will provide or approve the website's legal/policy language where applicable. I am not expecting the developer to provide legal advice or independently determine Gwenlightenment's legal obligations. I am expecting the developer to properly implement the provided policies, disclosures, consent mechanisms, privacy settings, and related technical functionality within the website.

Payment Processing + Security
I will select and provide the payment-processing system/gateway that will be used for Gwenlightenment. The developer will be responsible for properly integrating and configuring the selected payment system with the website's applicable checkout, product, membership, subscription, donation, and account functionality.

Payment-related functionality should be configured using appropriate security practices, and applicable payment, checkout, subscription, and account flows should be thoroughly tested before launch.
The website should not unnecessarily store raw credit/debit card information within WordPress.


DESIGN DIRECTION

This is extremely important to me.

I want Gwenlightenment to be: Beautiful. Warm. Earthy. Botanical. Whimsical. Soulful. Artistic. Feminine without being childish. Spiritual without looking cliché. Editorial without feeling corporate. Interactive without becoming overwhelming.

The website should feel almost like entering a digital garden, library, journal, apothecary, kitchen, sanctuary, and creative world at the same time.

I love details such as:
•	Botanical illustrations 
•	Pressed/floral imagery 
•	Handwritten notes 
•	Paper textures 
•	Organic section transitions 
•	Layered imagery 
•	Warm photography 
•	Books 
•	Plants 
•	Food 
•	Nature 
•	Soft earthy palettes 
•	Thoughtful typography 
•	Polaroid/journal elements 
•	Small discoveries throughout the page 
•	Gentle movement 
•	Beautiful hover interactions 
•	Organic shapes 
•	Intentional visual storytelling 

However, usability comes first. Visitors should never become confused because the website is artistic.
The goal is: unique enough to remember + intuitive enough to use effortlessly.


PERFORMANCE & DEVELOPMENT PHILOSOPHY

Because the visual direction includes imagery, texture, illustration, and interaction, I need someone who understands how to achieve this aesthetic without creating an unnecessarily slow or fragile website.

Please avoid:
•	Excessive plugin dependency 
•	Bloated page-builder implementations 
•	Huge unoptimized images 
•	Unnecessary animation libraries 
•	Hard-coded content that should be editable 
•	Fragile layouts 
•	Desktop-only design thinking 
•	Unlicensed assets 
•	Plugins/themes that cannot legally be transferred or maintained 
•	Systems that lock the site into your personal developer account 

Backups & Recovery: Configure an appropriate automated backup system for the production website, including database and website files, with a practical restoration/recovery process. 

The developer should confirm that backups are functioning before launch. The website and its core accounts/assets should ultimately remain under my ownership/control.


LONG-TERM OPPORTUNITY

I am not looking for someone to disappear immediately after launch.

If the full website project goes well, I would like to open another ongoing contract with the developer for long-term website maintenance, development, SEO, content support, and continued growth of Gwenlightenment.
I expect the website to continue expanding after launch, so I would strongly prefer to establish a long-term relationship with someone who already understands the website's architecture, branding, membership system, products, and overall vision.

Future work may include:
•	WordPress updates 
•	Plugin/theme maintenance 
•	Backups/security 
•	Troubleshooting 
•	Performance monitoring and optimization 
•	New products 
•	New pages 
•	New memberships 
•	New subscriptions 
•	New AI tools/integrations 
•	New classes 
•	Website improvements 
•	Seasonal Baked With Intention updates 
•	Email campaigns 
•	Product/class/content launches 
•	Launch support 
•	Conversion improvements 
•	New interactive features 
•	General technical support 
•	Ongoing SEO maintenance and optimization 
•	SEO optimization for new blog articles 
•	SEO optimization for new recipes, Herb Library entries, products, and pages 
•	Keyword and search-intent research 
•	Content SEO recommendations 
•	Internal-linking improvements 
•	Technical SEO monitoring 
•	Google Search Console monitoring 
•	Organic search performance monitoring 
•	Sitemap/indexing maintenance 
•	Crawl-error monitoring and resolution 
•	Broken-link monitoring 
•	Redirect management 
•	Schema/structured-data maintenance 
•	Updating and optimizing older content 
•	Basic SEO reporting/analytics 
•	Local SEO support where applicable 
•	Recommendations for improving Gwenlightenment's search visibility and organic growth over time 

I would strongly prefer to find someone I can continue working with as Gwenlightenment grows rather than hiring a different developer every time something needs to be added or changed.

Please let me know whether you are interested in this type of ongoing relationship and what types of maintenance, development, SEO, and website-growth services you normally provide after launch.


WHO I AM LOOKING FOR

You may be a good fit if you:
•	Have strong WordPress development experience 
•	Have a strong eye for design 
•	Can work from detailed briefs without needing every pixel dictated 
•	Enjoy creative/non-corporate websites 
•	Can build custom functionality when appropriate 
•	Understand e-commerce and memberships 
•	Understand dynamic content architecture 
•	Understand responsive design 
•	Can balance aesthetics with performance 
•	Communicate clearly 
•	Are comfortable receiving detailed feedback 
•	Think ahead instead of only building what is directly in front of you 
•	Can recommend better technical solutions when you see them 
•	Care about the backend experience as much as the frontend 
•	Can build something designed to grow for years 
•	Understands WordPress SEO and can implement a technically sound SEO foundation during the initial website build. 
•	Has experience with on-page SEO, technical SEO, content SEO, and basic keyword/search-intent research. 
•	Understands SEO for content-heavy websites containing articles, recipes, products, categories, and growing resource libraries. 
•	Understands Google Search Console, XML sitemaps, indexing/crawl management, metadata, internal linking, redirects, and schema/structured data. 
•	Understands how WordPress architecture, site performance, mobile responsiveness, and content structure affect SEO. 
•	Can build reusable article/recipe/product structures that remain SEO-friendly as new content is published. 
•	Is interested in providing ongoing SEO monitoring and optimization after launch. 
•	Local SEO experience is a plus because Baked With Intention will include local ordering/pickup in the San Antonio/New Braunfels, Texas area.

I am especially interested in developers who have previously built: membership sites, editorial/content-heavy websites, recipe websites, WooCommerce stores, subscription websites, highly designed WordPress sites, or websites containing custom interactive features.

Experience successfully managing SEO for a growing WordPress website—particularly an editorial, recipe, e-commerce, membership, wellness, lifestyle, or other content-heavy website—is a strong plus.


HOW TO APPLY
Please include the following in your proposal:

1. Your portfolio
Send me links to actual live WordPress websites you personally built or substantially developed.
Please specify what you personally did on each project.

2. Your closest comparable project
Which project in your portfolio is most similar to Gwenlightenment in terms of design complexity, membership/e-commerce functionality, or scale?

3. Test-page price
My intended budget is $100–$150 fixed price.
Tell me your price within that range.

4. Estimated full website price
Please provide your own estimate/quote for building the complete website described above. I want applicants to price the project based on the actual scope and their normal rates.

Please separate, if possible:
Estimated development/build cost
and
estimated third-party costs such as premium plugins, software licenses, email platforms, hosting upgrades, APIs, etc.

5. Estimated timeline
Please estimate:
•	Start Here test-page turnaround 
•	Full website development timeline 
•	Approximate availability/start date 

6. Ongoing maintenance
Tell me whether you are interested in continuing after launch and how you normally price ongoing maintenance/support.

7. Maintenance/editability
Briefly explain how you would structure the backend so I can easily add articles, recipes, weekly menus, products, books, recommendations, etc. myself.


PLEASE BEGIN YOUR PROPOSAL WITH:
“A KINDER YOU CREATES A KINDER WORLD.”

This lets me know you actually read the project description/contract before applying.

Generic/copy-pasted proposals that do not address the project will not be considered.


TEST PROJECT BUDGET

$100–$150 fixed price

This contract is specifically for development of the Start Here page only.

The full Gwenlightenment website will be negotiated separately with the developer I choose after the test.
If I select the test developer for the complete project, the amount paid for the test page will be credited toward the mutually agreed full-site development price.


PROJECT GOAL

I am not simply trying to hire someone to "make me a website."

I am looking for someone who can help turn Gwenlightenment into a beautiful, functional, scalable digital world that people can explore for years as the project grows.

The first page is the test.

If we work beautifully together, I hope the rest of Gwenlightenment—and a long-term working relationship—comes after it.

title: Website building
description:
We are looking for an experienced website designer/developer to build a professional, modern, and easy-to-manage website for our local dance/fitness studio and event rental space.

We are NOT necessarily looking for a completely custom-coded website. We are open to using an established platform and integrations if that will give us the functionality we need while keeping the website affordable, secure, and easy for us to maintain ourselves.

Our goal is to create one central website that serves our clients, instructors, and event-rental customers.

WEBSITE FEATURES

• Professional, modern, mobile-friendly website

• Studio information, photos, location, FAQs, reviews/testimonials, instructor information, etc.

• Live class calendar that can easily be updated as classes are added, changed, or canceled

• Clients should be able to view classes and sign up/register

• Individual class listings should include information such as instructor, date/time, class description, price, availability, and registration/payment link

INSTRUCTOR ACCOUNTS & CLASS MANAGEMENT

We would ideally like instructors to have individual accounts with limited permissions.

Instructors should be able to:

• Log into their own account

• Add and manage their own classes

• Update class descriptions, dates, times, pricing, etc.

• Add their own registration/payment link

• Access studio policies, agreements, forms, and resources

Instructors should NOT have access to other instructors’ private information or the overall administrative side of the website.

PAYMENTS

We specifically do NOT want our business collecting class fees on behalf of individual instructors.

Each instructor should be able to connect or provide their own outside registration/payment link so their class payments go directly to them.

The studio does need the ability to collect payments that belong directly to the studio, such as:

• Instructor studio rental fees

• Event rental fees/deposits if we decide to accept those online

These payments should go directly to our business payment processor/account.

INSTRUCTOR ONBOARDING & DOCUMENT MANAGEMENT

We would like an instructor onboarding system or portal that allows us to send a new instructor one link and have them complete the required onboarding process.

This should ideally include:

• Electronic instructor agreements/contracts

• Electronic liability waiver

• Studio policies/forms

• Proof/certificate of insurance upload

• Certification/CPR or other credential uploads when applicable

• Other required instructor documentation

If sensitive identification documents are ever required, such as a driver’s license, we do NOT want these stored in a standard website media/file library. We would want a secure document-management solution with appropriate encryption, access controls, and privacy protections.

We would like an administrative dashboard or similar system where we can quickly see each instructor’s onboarding status, for example:

Agreement – Complete
Liability Waiver – Complete
Insurance – Complete
CPR/Certification – Complete

It would also be very helpful to track expiration dates for insurance, CPR, certifications, etc. and receive reminders when updated documentation is needed.

CLIENT LIABILITY WAIVERS

We would like clients/participants to be able to electronically sign our studio liability waiver.

The system should maintain a record of completed waivers so we can verify whether someone has a current waiver on file.

Because we offer children’s classes, we also need an appropriate process for a parent/legal guardian to sign on behalf of a minor.

EVENT RENTAL SECTION

Our studio is also available as an event rental venue.

We would like a separate section of the website dedicated to event rentals that can include:

• Photos of the space

• Amenities

• Rental information and/or pricing

• FAQs

• Contact Us / Request More Information form

• Potential availability/inquiry functionality

• Electronic event rental agreement and waiver, if appropriate

ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENTS

One of our biggest priorities is ease of use after the website is completed.

We need to be able to manage normal day-to-day updates ourselves without contacting a developer every time something changes.

Owners/admins should be able to easily:

• Add/edit/remove classes

• Add/remove instructors

• Update schedules

• Update photos and website content

• Change pricing/information

• Review registrations when applicable

• Review instructor onboarding/document status

• Review signed waivers

• Manage event rental information

The website must work extremely well on mobile devices since we expect many customers to access it from their phones.

WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

When submitting your proposal, please include:

1. Examples of similar websites you have built, especially dance studios, fitness studios, yoga/Pilates studios, class-based businesses, membership systems, or event venues.
2. The platform you recommend for this project and WHY you recommend it.
3. How you would build the live class calendar and registration system.
4. How you would allow instructors to manage their own classes without giving them full website access.
5. How you would structure payments so individual instructors receive their class payments directly while the studio separately receives its rental/event payments.
6. What system you recommend for electronic contracts and liability waivers.
7. How you recommend handling secure instructor document uploads and storage.
8. Whether/how the system can track expiration dates for insurance and certifications.
9. Your estimated timeline from start to launch.
10. Your estimated TOTAL project cost.
11. A breakdown of any ongoing expenses we should expect, including hosting, software, scheduling/booking systems, payment processing, e-signatures, document storage, plugins, or other monthly/annual fees.
12. What ongoing maintenance, if any, you believe would require a developer after launch.

We are looking for someone who can recommend the RIGHT solution rather than automatically building everything from scratch.

The finished website should be professional and polished for our customers while being simple and practical for us to operate behind the scenes.

Please begin your proposal by telling us which platform/system you would recommend for this project and why. This will help us identify applicants who have reviewed the full project requirements
coverLetter:
Hi! I recommend WordPress paired with custom user roles and Gravity Forms, as it avoids high monthly platform fees while giving you total control over instructor permissions without custom-coding from scratch.

Using WordPress, we can create restricted instructor accounts so they only manage their own class listings and insert their own direct payment links. I’ll set up secure e-signatures for client waivers (including parent/guardian signing for minors) and route sensitive onboarding documents to encrypted, non-media cloud storage with automated expiration reminders for CPR and insurance updates. Studio rental payments will route directly to your separate studio merchant account. Having developed custom membership and resource portals like https://www.daysforgirls.org/, I will ensure the site is easy for your team to manage.

title: Senior WordPress + WooCommerce Engineer - Documented Technical Remediation Across 9 Live Sites
description:
Senior WordPress / WooCommerce engineer needed to fix a documented technical debt backlog across a nine-site estate. This is remediation engineering against a defect register we already own, not an SEO content or marketing engagement.

ABOUT US
Duraamen Engineered Products manufactures and supplies specialty flooring systems — microcement, urethane concrete, epoxy and polished-concrete products — sold to contractors and specifiers across the United States and the GCC. We run nine WordPress installs: a primary corporate site with a WooCommerce store, five regional market sites, a UAE site, a separate microcement brand, and a contractor directory. Hosting is WP Engine, fronted by Cloudflare.

WHAT WE HAVE ALREADY DONE
In September 2026 we commissioned an independent crawl of every URL in every sitemap across the estate — 2,160 pages — and recorded 9,177 defects itemised per URL with severity. We then reconciled 12,279 historically archived URLs against the current sitemaps and re-tested the critical findings live. You are not being asked to discover the problems. They are documented, with URLs, in the attached work package.
WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG (all verified)
•	Zero of 204 WooCommerce shop, product and product-category URLs carry Product schema. No Product, no Offer, no AggregateRating — while Google Listings & Ads and Facebook for WooCommerce are both installed and active.
•	A contractor-directory template returns a live, indexable HTTP 200 page for any arbitrary string in one URL segment. An unbounded crawl trap. Its canonical output is cache-variant: the same URL returns a broken template token, no canonical, or the correct value on different requests.
•	Roughly 1,600 historical URLs return 404 with no redirect. Four site rebuilds since 2009 and no redirect map was ever built. The affected set includes article URLs from 2019 through 2025, not just old ones.
•	433 pages have no H1 element. 759 have more than one, some with 15 to 17. Verified identical across browser, Googlebot and neutral user agents, so this is template-level, not a rendering artefact.
•	74 internal links on live pages point at hard 404s. A further 747 point at redirecting URLs. 753 point at WordPress attachment pages.
•	1,107 pages have no meta description. 9,714 images have no alt attribute. The primary site serves 43 WebP images out of 20,580.
•	Two regional sites carry no LocalBusiness schema at all — they are typed as Article with a Person author.
•	The primary site's homepage loads 79 CSS files and 97 JS files, 5.36 MB across 178 requests, with no page-caching plugin and Cloudflare bypassing HTML. It also runs two Advanced Coupons builds, three freight-quote plugins and two cookie-consent plugins simultaneously.
•	One WordPress install on our primary domain has been unmaintained since 2023 and is fully indexable. We treat that as a security finding first.
THE WORK, IN THREE MILESTONES
Milestone 1 — Day 1 to 15. Verified backups and staging clones for every site with a tested rollback path. Baseline capture from Search Console and analytics, signed off before anything changes. Then indexation integrity: kill the crawl trap at the rewrite-rule level, make canonical output deterministic against a purged cache, clean the sitemaps, remove stale and competing sitemap files, remove Crawl-delay directives, resolve origin instability.
Milestone 2 — Day 16 to 30. Product and Offer schema across all 204 commercial URLs at template level. Complete per-market LocalBusiness markup. Fix the H1 defects in the theme templates, not page by page. Metadata remediation at volume. Decide and implement the handling of 214 near-duplicate product-tag archives. Reciprocal hreflang with x-default.
Milestone 3 — Day 31 to 45. Deploy the 301 redirect map for the dead historical URLs, no chains, no blanket homepage redirects. Repair the internal link defects. Image alt and WebP programme. Front-end payload, caching and Core Web Vitals to a pass on mobile. Then a full re-crawl and a Search Console comparison against the Day-1 baseline.

HOW WE WORK — NON-NEGOTIABLE
•	Nothing touches production without a verified backup, a staging test and a post-deploy smoke test.
•	Every change is logged: date, site, component, version, staging result, production result, rollback status.
•	No task is complete on assertion. It is complete when it is live, re-tested, and evidenced with URLs, crawl output and Search Console data.
•	No purchased links, no auto-translated content, no placeholder or duplicated location-template copy.
•	We own all code, credentials and documentation produced. Anything custom you write is documented in writing before final payment.

Acceptance on the final milestone is an independent re-crawl we commission, showing zero Critical and zero High defects within scope. A portion of the final milestone is withheld until that re-crawl passes. We would rather tell you that now than surprise you later.

WHAT YOUR PROPOSAL MUST INCLUDE
Start your proposal with the word "Canonical" so we know you read this.
1.	Two or three WooCommerce sites you have worked on, with URLs, and what you specifically did on each.
2.	A time you fixed a schema or structured-data problem at template level across hundreds of URLs — how you did it, and whether you used a plugin or wrote it.
3.	Your experience with WP Engine and Cloudflare together, specifically cache behaviour and purge control.
4.	Your approach to building and deploying a redirect map of roughly 1,600 rows — at what layer, and how you would test it.
5.	Whether you work alone or with a team. If a team, who does what.
6.	Your fixed price per milestone, and the delivery window you commit to for each.
7.	Your time zone and your overlap with US Eastern.
We will not evaluate proposals that quote a single blended figure without milestone breakdown, or that ignore the attached work package.

The full per-URL defect register — 9,177 rows in a spreadsheet — goes to shortlisted candidates. The attached work package is the scope you should price against.
