title: Custom WordPress dentist directory - migrate off a plugin, rebuild US city pages
description:
We already run a US dentist directory on WordPress. It was built with a location-page plugin and has tens of thousands of city/state URLs.

Search is broken: location URLs canonicalize to a parent hub, invented slugs return 200 instead of 404, and most pages are thin templates. We want a custom directory. No GeoDirectory, ListingPro, or other city-page plugin.

What we need:
- Custom WordPress: states, cities, practices, and which practices serve which cities
- City and listing templates
- Bulk import of dentists, not building the list by hand. Ingest practices that match how patients search: emergency, walk-in, after-hours, 24-hour. Store those attributes so city pages can filter and display them
- Published city pages should show at least five matching practices. 
- City copy that is actually local: landmarks, neighborhoods, after-hours context. Shared boilerplate under about 40% of the page

Technical bar:
- Only published locations get a live URL. Fake city/state/page slugs return 404
- Published city and practice URLs self-canonical, not to a hub
- Sitemap of indexable URLs only
- Migration off the current URL set: 301 pages worth keeping, 410/404 the rest. Do not mass-redirect tens of thousands of thin URLs onto a few hubs
- Remove the old plugin after cutover

Done when cities are filled from an import, pages have distinct local copy, self-canonical, and sit in the sitemap; a fake slug 404s; the old plugin is gone.

To apply, answer all of these:
1. A custom WP directory you built (not an off-the-shelf directory plugin). What did the URLs look like?
2. How have you migrated a large plugin-generated URL set without wrecking indexation?
3. How do you 404 unknown slugs and keep published URLs self-canonical?
4. How would you import dentists at US scale and tag emergency / walk-in / after-hours / 24-hour without inventing listings? What data source or method would you use?
5. How would you keep each city page unique and valuable so pages do not share more than about 40% of the copy?

title: Senior WooCommerce + Google Merchant Center Developer Needed – GLA / Sale Price Sync Debugging
description:
We are looking for a senior WooCommerce developer with genuine hands-on experience debugging Google Merchant Center / Google for WooCommerce (formerly Google Listings & Ads) product-price synchronisation issues.

This is not a Google Ads management, SEO, basic Merchant Center setup, or general WordPress job.

I specifically need someone who understands the technical path between:

WooCommerce product pricing
Google for WooCommerce / Google Listings & Ads (GLA)
Google Merchant Center
Content API / Merchant API
WordPress Action Scheduler / WP-Cron
WooCommerce price hooks/filters
Custom pricing/API integrations
PHP-level debugging

I already have an experienced WooCommerce developer investigating the issue. His work has been excellent and he is actively working on it.

However, because this pricing problem is currently affecting our Google Shopping advertising and ability to generate sales, I would like a second experienced pair of eyes with specific WooCommerce → Google Merchant Center integration experience.

The initial engagement will be diagnosis/review only.

I do not want two developers simultaneously making changes to the production website. I want an independent technical assessment first.

If your investigation identifies the cause and we agree on the solution, I would be happy to extend the contract to implementation and potentially ongoing/long-term WooCommerce development work.

Current problem

We operate a WooCommerce store with approximately 130 products and a custom pricing setup that uses Amazon pricing data as part of calculating our selling prices.

WooCommerce and the customer-facing website can currently contain the correct customer-facing prices.

However, we are experiencing an intermittent issue where Google Merchant Center receives the regular price correctly but loses or fails to receive the WooCommerce sale_price for some products.

For example, one product should contain:

Regular price: £238.68
Sale/customer-facing price: £187.99

Following certain synchronisations, Merchant Center correctly receives both values:

price = £238.68
sale_price = £187.99

However, later the sale_price can disappear from Merchant Center, leaving only the £238.68 regular price.

Google Shopping/Ads can therefore advertise the wrong price even though the website itself is displaying the correct customer-facing price.

This behaviour is inconsistent across the catalogue.

At one point, approximately 35–40% of products had the correct sale price populated in Merchant Center while the remainder did not.

We have also observed an important pattern:

Products can become correct following one scheduled synchronisation and subsequently become incorrect again.

Relevant history – WooCommerce performance work

There is important background that may or may not be related.

Earlier this year, our existing developer carried out a detailed WooCommerce performance audit of the website.

The audit identified significant backend activity, including unusually heavy scheduled/background processing associated with Google Listings & Ads / Google for WooCommerce.

Following the audit, several performance/backend changes were implemented to improve the reliability and performance of the website.

This included work relating to areas such as:

WordPress/WooCommerce scheduled jobs
Action Scheduler / cron behaviour
Google for WooCommerce synchronisation activity
Caching/performance
Database/query performance
Other WooCommerce backend optimisation

The performance work itself successfully improved the website.

I want to make clear that I am not claiming these changes caused the subsequent pricing problems.

However, the chronology is relevant because I was not experiencing these recurring pricing/synchronisation problems before this period of backend work.

I therefore want the relationship, if any, independently investigated rather than assumed.

First pricing problem – WooCommerce prices dropping approximately 20%

After the performance/backend work, we began experiencing a recurring WooCommerce pricing issue.

Approximately every 3–4 days, virtually all of our in-stock products would suddenly drop in price by roughly 20%.

Our external Amazon pricing system/database still contained the correct calculated prices, but the prices actually stored/displayed by WooCommerce became incorrect.

Importantly, manually rerunning our price-sync jobs would immediately restore the correct WooCommerce prices.

Our existing developer investigated this and was able to reproduce the behaviour on staging.

The investigation initially identified behaviour involving the Import Products from Amazon plugin.

Further investigation indicated that there appeared to be a loop/interference between our Amazon pricing synchronisation and an older discount/pricing plugin.

During certain price reads, the discount logic appeared capable of returning a figure approximately 20% too low. The synchronisation process could then save that value back into WooCommerce.

This explained why:

many products changed at approximately the same time;
the change was approximately the same percentage;
our external pricing system still contained the correct values; and
manually rerunning the price synchronisation immediately corrected WooCommerce.

Changes were subsequently made to prevent the discount logic from affecting those price reads.

The recurring ~20% WooCommerce price-drop problem now appears to have been resolved.

What happened afterwards – Google Merchant Center mismatch

After the WooCommerce pricing problem was corrected, we subsequently began experiencing the current Google Merchant Center pricing problem.

The distinction is important:

Previously, WooCommerce itself was receiving/storing incorrect prices.

Now, WooCommerce and the customer-facing website can have the correct price, while Google Merchant Center receives a different representation of the product.

In particular, Merchant Center may receive the regular price but fail to retain/receive sale_price.

For some products, a scheduled sync restores the correct sale_price.

Later, something appears capable of causing that sale price to disappear again.

What our existing developer has found so far

Our current developer has confirmed that scheduled feed synchronisation is capable of producing the correct sale prices.

For example, he verified products where Merchant Center correctly received the expected customer-facing sale_price.

However, something subsequently appears capable of stripping, omitting or failing to supply sale_price for certain products.

His current working theory is that Google may be obtaining product data from the website/WooCommerce through another channel or synchronisation path that isn't seeing the discount/sale price correctly, triggering later updates with different pricing data.

He has now added logging intended to identify which channel/process is responsible.

I do not want applicants simply to accept this theory.

I want an independent senior developer to review the evidence and architecture and reach their own technical conclusion.

Why I am providing the full history

The chronology currently looks roughly like this:

WooCommerce performance/backend optimisation

→ Recurring ~20% WooCommerce pricing problem

→ Pricing-read/discount interaction identified and changed

→ WooCommerce pricing stabilised

→ Intermittent Google Merchant Center sale_price problem

This sequence may be connected or it may be coincidental.

I specifically do not want someone to assume causation simply because of the chronology.

Instead, I want someone capable of determining whether changes involving WooCommerce price getters/hooks, discount logic, our Amazon synchronisation, Action Scheduler/cron, Google for WooCommerce/GLA or another product-data pathway could result in different systems receiving different representations of the same WooCommerce product price.

What I need investigated

The initial task is diagnosis/review.

I can provide:

Screenshots and examples
Merchant Center access if required
Previous developer findings
The previous WooCommerce performance audit
Examples of affected products
Details of the Amazon pricing integration
Merchant Center product exports
Relevant information from the existing developer's investigation

I would like you to determine:

Every process/channel capable of supplying or updating our product pricing in Google Merchant Center.
Why sale_price is present following some synchronisations but missing following others.
Whether the issue originates from:
WooCommerce itself
Google for WooCommerce / GLA
Content API / Merchant API
WooCommerce hooks or filters
Our custom Amazon pricing integration
The previous discount/pricing logic
Action Scheduler / WP-Cron
Google's own website/product-data retrieval
Cached/stale product data
Or an interaction between multiple systems.
Whether the previous WooCommerce pricing issue and the current Merchant Center issue are technically connected.
Exactly what process is responsible for causing Merchant Center to lose/fail to receive sale_price.
What you recommend as a permanent fix.
How the pricing architecture could be made more reliable so that WooCommerce, the website, Merchant Center, Google Shopping and other integrations consistently receive the same intended customer-facing price.
Experience I'm specifically looking for

Ideally, you have personally debugged problems involving several of the following:

WooCommerce regular_price, sale_price and active _price
WooCommerce price getters, hooks and filters
Google for WooCommerce / Google Listings & Ads
Google Merchant Center
Content API / Merchant API
WooCommerce → Google product synchronisation
WordPress Action Scheduler
WP-Cron
Custom/dynamic WooCommerce pricing
REST APIs
Third-party WooCommerce integrations
PHP-level debugging and instrumentation
WooCommerce product metadata
Background/scheduled product updates
Intermittent product-feed/synchronisation problems

I am particularly interested in developers who have previously dealt with situations where Merchant Center intermittently receives the regular price but loses, overwrites or fails to receive sale_price.

Please do NOT apply if...

Your experience is primarily:

Google Ads campaign management
PPC
SEO
Basic Merchant Center account setup
Basic product-feed configuration
General WordPress website building
Installing/configuring WooCommerce plugins

This problem requires someone comfortable going underneath the plugin interfaces and tracing behaviour at the WooCommerce/PHP/API/Action Scheduler level.

Initial engagement

This will initially be an hourly diagnosis/review engagement.

I would prefer to begin with approximately 3–5 hours of investigation.

At this stage, I primarily want you to:

Investigate → identify likely/root cause → document your findings → recommend the fix.

Please do not make changes to the production pricing system without my approval.

My existing developer is still actively investigating the issue, so I do not want two people independently modifying the same system at the same time.

If your diagnosis identifies the problem and we agree on the approach, I can then authorise implementation.

There is also the possibility of a long-term working relationship for someone with strong WooCommerce/backend/integration expertise.

IMPORTANT – please answer this when applying

Please start your proposal by answering the following:

Have you personally debugged a WooCommerce → Google Merchant Center issue where sale_price was intermittently missing, overwritten, removed or different depending on the sync/API path?

If yes, briefly explain:

What caused it, how you identified it, and how you fixed it.

Then please explain how you would approach identifying:

Which WooCommerce hook, scheduled action, API request, Google for WooCommerce process or other synchronisation path is causing sale_price to disappear in this case?

Please be specific.

I'm much more interested in your actual debugging methodology and relevant experience than a generic proposal about how many years you've worked with WordPress.

title: WordPress Developer to Launch HR Consulting Site — WooCommerce, Stripe & Forms
description:
WordPress Developer to Launch 18-Page HR Consulting Site — WooCommerce, Stripe & Forms

About us

Urban Human Resources is an HR consulting and career strategy practice in Oakland, California. We serve companies that need an HR function without hiring a department, and individual professionals working on their careers. The site is our primary sales channel, so it needs to work correctly on day one.

The project

A complete 18-page site already exists. It was designed and built in Claude Design and exports as clean, self-contained HTML with inline styles, plus a shared header and footer used across every page. Every page is finished, written and responsive, with structured data already in place. There is no build step, no framework and no dependencies to install — the files open in a browser as they are.

We are not asking you to design anything or write any copy.

What the site cannot do is talk to a server, because it is static. We need it implemented on WordPress and eleven specific things made functional. The full list is below and in the attached spec.

We host with Bluehost on WordPress. Stripe is our only payment processor and will stay that way — please do not propose PayPal, Square or an alternative gateway.

What needs to be built

Implement the 18 pages on WordPress — preserving layout, type, spacing and colors exactly, and keeping the existing JobPosting, FAQPage, Service and Product schema intact. The site was built for search and answer-engine visibility and we do not want that lost.
A WooCommerce cart — 27 products: 2 subscriptions, 4 services, 6 digital templates, 14 merchandise items, 1 free download. Products already exist in our Stripe account; reuse them. Today each item links to its own Stripe Payment Link and buyers cannot combine items.
Recurring billing for two subscriptions — $4.99/month membership and $1,999/month retainer. Core WooCommerce does not do this; tell us in your proposal how you would handle it and what it costs.
Stripe customer portal enabled — so subscribers cancel and update cards themselves instead of emailing us.
Automatic digital delivery — six paid templates plus one free download. We supply the files; buyers should receive them on payment without us touching anything.
Correct tax codes by product type — everything currently carries one physical-goods code, which is wrong for services, digital goods and the membership.
Seven forms wired up — consult request, job application with resume upload, newsletter signup, and four lead-magnet email captures. All seven currently validate and confirm on screen, then discard the data.
Four lead magnets delivered by autoresponder — a resume audit, a California compliance checklist, an exempt vs. non-exempt quick check and a free store download. Each promises a PDF by email. We supply the files.
Newsletter connected to a mail service — Mailchimp, Kit or Brevo, with double opt-in and unsubscribe. Our privacy policy already commits to this.
A scheduler on the contact page — Calendly, Cal.com or similar. The FAQ tells clients sessions are booked on a booking link and none exists yet.
Membership access gated — paying $4.99 currently grants nothing enforced. We plan to share a Google Drive folder; tell us whether you would gate it in WordPress instead, and how cancellations would revoke access.
Also carry over intact

Dark mode toggle with persistence. Header dropdown menus and mobile drawer. On-site search over page content and page sections. Two SociableKit feed widgets (HR news RSS and Instagram), one styled into a narrow homepage sidebar. A retention rule on job application data — our privacy policy commits to deleting resumes after twelve months. And pick one source for sitemap.xml and robots.txt; we have static files at the root and an SEO plugin would generate its own.

Launch checks before handover

SSL, admin 2FA, a backup routine, Google Search Console verified and the sitemap submitted, and test purchases run across all four product types.

What you get from us

All 18 pages and the shared header and footer as finished HTML with assets. A written spec covering the full product list, categories, shipping rule, tax codes and delivery settings. Stripe and Bluehost access. Direct access to the owner for decisions, usually same-day.

Required experience

Proven WooCommerce builds with the Stripe gateway — please link two live stores you have built
Recurring billing or subscription commerce
Implementing supplied designs faithfully rather than substituting a theme
Digital-product delivery and tax configuration
Clear written English and a predictable weekly update
Nice to have

Professional services or consulting clients. Technical SEO: schema preservation, Core Web Vitals, Search Console. Accessibility (WCAG AA) awareness.

How we would like to run it

We would prefer to work in four milestones rather than one lump contract, so both sides can see progress early:

Port three pages — Home, Store and Contact — proving the design and schema carry over faithfully
The remaining 15 pages, plus dark mode, navigation, search and the feed widgets
WooCommerce with all 27 products, shipping and physical merchandise
Subscriptions, digital delivery, tax codes and the membership gate
Propose a price per milestone. If you would rather structure it differently, tell us why.

Project details

One project, roughly 3–4 weeks. Fixed-price per milestone preferred. Start immediately. We are reviewing several proposals and will pick on demonstrated WooCommerce and Stripe experience rather than on price alone.

In your proposal, please answer

Two live WooCommerce stores you built, with the Stripe integration visible
How you would handle the two recurring subscriptions, and what it costs
Your approach to implementing supplied HTML on WordPress — page builder, custom theme or block templates, and why
Your total fixed price and the milestones
What you need from us before you can start
Please do not send a generic proposal. Reference something specific from this post so we know you read it.

The milestone structure does double duty: it protects you with any hire, and the last line about picking on experience rather than price discourages the race-to-the-bottom bids without you having to name a budget.

• Improving button sizing, placement and tap accessibility
• Checking the mobile navigation, header and footer

• Your fixed total price

title: WordPress Document Automation  – WPForms, E2PDF & Stripe

Document 2 – 5 pages
Document 3 – 10 pages

The primary issue is formatting. The automated output needs to look like a professionally prepared legal document, not raw generated output.

I am attaching one document that contains a side-by-side comparison of the 10-page automated document. The current automated version is shown on the left, and the professionally formatted version I produce for clients is shown on the right. The specific formatting issues I want corrected are listed on pages 11–14 of that same attachment.

I am specifically looking for someone who already knows WPForms, E2PDF, Stripe, document automation, conditional logic, and professional PDF/document formatting. I am not interested in paying someone to learn these systems while working on my project.

Please do not propose rebuilding my website or moving everything to another platform unless there is a legitimate technical reason the existing system cannot work.

This will be a fixed-price project with milestone payments tied to actual completion:

Milestone 1 – First 5-page document fully corrected, tested, and live: $150

Milestone 2 – Second 5-page document fully corrected, tested, and live: $150

Milestone 3 – 10-page document fully corrected, tested, and live: $200

Total project budget: $500.

Each milestone will be approved only after the document has been tested from the public-facing form through payment, generation, and delivery and is functioning properly.

I have additional legal documents I want to automate once these three are successfully completed. If you are a good fit, communicate well, and complete these properly, I will have additional ongoing work available.

When applying, please confirm your direct experience with WPForms, E2PDF, Stripe, document automation, conditional logic, and formatting generated documents to closely match professionally formatted Word documents. title: Urgent WordPress malware cleanup needed for persistent PHP/auto_prepend infection
description:
I need an experienced WordPress malware/security specialist to clean a hacked WordPress site on Namecheap shared hosting.

This is not a simple plugin issue. Known symptoms/findings:
- Browser DevTools shows an injected request to https://forecast-chaos.com/x9i32md/w1/la02
- Malware injects obfuscated inline JavaScript into the homepage
- Malicious MU-plugin found at /wp-content/mu-plugins/vista-tracker-ops.php
- .user.ini and .htaccess were repeatedly rewritten with auto_prepend_file
- Payload files included /wp-content/ed34bae7.php, /wp-content/.ed34bae7.php, and /wp-content/81b7e91f.php
- Fake/suspicious plugin wordpesso was found and removed
- Imunify360 detected/cleaned backdoor-related files including /wp-content/.sc_15c1a847/core_d1ac14b9.php
- The infection has recreated files after WordPress/PHP was triggered

I need someone who can:
- Find and remove the persistence/backdoor source, not just delete visible malware files
- Inspect .user.ini, .htaccess, MU-plugins, wp-content, plugins/themes, uploads, and access logs
- Repair or replace infected WordPress core/plugin/theme files safely
- Keep the site working if possible
- Provide a clear list of files changed/removed and recommended next steps
- Advise on credential resets and hardening after cleanup

Please reply with:
1. Your experience with WordPress auto_prepend_file malware/backdoors
2. How you would approach this case

* Their desktop and mobile menus
* Clean navigation and information hierarchy
* Services and locations structure
* Strong imagery and typography
* Modern/editorial appearance
* Easy booking journey
* How the website accommodates many services and locations without feeling cluttered

For Exhale, we envisage a premium private healthcare aesthetic using deep teal/dark green, warm off-white/ivory, charcoal and subtle brass/gold accents, together with high quality real clinic photography/video.

The finished website should feel modern, confident and premium — not like a generic medical WordPress template.

WEBSITE STRUCTURE

We would like a scalable structure broadly covering:

TREATMENTS
Osteopathy, Physiotherapy, Sports Massage, Cranial Osteopathy, Baby/Paediatric Osteopathy, Pregnancy Osteopathy, Acupuncture and Laser Therapy.

WHAT WE TREAT
Back pain, neck pain, sciatica, shoulder/hip/knee problems, sports injuries, headaches/TMJ and other conditions.

BABIES & CHILDREN
This is an important specialist area for us and should have its own prominent section.

LOCATIONS
Sutton Coldfield and Lichfield initially, but the website must make it easy to add future locations such as Birmingham.

OUR TEAM
Individual practitioner profiles with services, specialist interests, locations and booking links.

ADVICE / KNOWLEDGE
A section for useful patient guides, articles, videos and future SEO content.

BOOKING

We use Cliniko and want booking integrated cleanly throughout the website, with particularly strong mobile booking UX.

SEO

* SEO-friendly site and URL architecture
* Multi-location SEO
* Good internal linking
* Proper heading structure
* Fast performance/Core Web Vitals
* Schema/basic technical SEO

We want reusable templates/components for areas such as treatments, conditions, locations and practitioner profiles so we can easily expand the website ourselves.

We must own the complete website, WordPress installation and design when the project is finished. No proprietary platform or ongoing lock-in.

INITIAL PROJECT

We are looking for someone who can:

* Help refine the sitemap/UX
* Create a premium visual design
* Build the site in WordPress
* Create excellent desktop and mobile navigation
* Create reusable page templates
* Integrate Cliniko booking
* Ensure the technical foundation is SEO-friendly
* Build/test on staging
* Assist with a safe migration to the existing domain

We are looking for a talented designer/developer who can create an original, premium Exhale website with excellent UX and a strong foundation for future SEO and growth.

There is likely to be ongoing work as we add further content, functionality and locations.

Visitors scan a QR code on-site, land on a subpage for a specific section of the landmark (e.g. Picture next to the main entry of the building), select their language via flag icons, read/listen to the explanation, and can optionally leave a rating/comment which is not visible for other website viewer.
There should be one single subpage per association/institution with a predefined template for each and every interesting element (like picture next to the main entry). 


Current status: 
hosting is live, WordPress is installed, HTTPS is set up, and the following plugins are already installed and activated: Elementor Pro, Polylang, Site Reviews, Pretty Links, UpdraftPlus, Code Snippets. All 7 languages are already set up in Polylang (DE, EN, TR, AL, MK, BS, MS). A first attempt at the header (flag language switcher) exists but is not finished/live yet.


Important: 
I have no web design experience. After this project, I only want to add content myself (text, photos, audio files) via Elementor — the structure/templates need to be fully finished and functional.


One Landing Page:
- Placeholder for some content
- Switch the language with Polylang
- Whenever one new sight-seeing is published it should be visible as a preview in the landing page (last 3 new sightseeings).
- Possibity to search: First country (just the one where minimum one sight seeing already exists (e.g. Germany). Then just the cities where we have already minium sight seeing (e.g. Hamburg), then all names of the sightseeing to open the subpage of that sightseeing.
These three information are visible in the linktree of the website: e.g. www.abc.com/germany/hamburg/harbour


Scope of Work

1. Header (global, via Elementor Theme Builder)
Flag-based language switcher (Polylang), top left or right, working for all 7 languages (more langues might follow later)
Below/next to it, a breadcrumb line: Country / City / Institute
Clean, simple design (not a generic demo layout)

2. Page template for one "Section" (as a reusable Elementor template)
Each subpage (= one sightseeing) needs:
Subpage header (e.g. "harbour")

Title: Entry to main building
Photo carousel (1–3 images with captions)
Audio player (for an uploaded MP3 file)
Text block for reading along
Star rating + comment field including optional image upload (plugin: Site Reviews) – comments/images should NOT be published publicly, only sent to a contact email address (configurable per landmark)
The template must be easy to duplicate, so I can swap out text/image/audio per language/section without rebuilding the layout

3. Link/QR preparation to jump directly to that part of the subpage.
Set up 10 Pretty Links pointing to the (placeholder-content) subpages, plus a short explanation of how I can create additional links myself

4. Handover
A short video guide (English) explaining how I, as a beginner, can:
create a new section page from the template
add text per language
swap out photos/audio
create a new Pretty Link


Technical Environment:
Hosting: All-Inkl
WordPress + Elementor Pro (Theme: Hello Elementor)
Multilingual: Polylang (already configured with 7 languages)
Ratings/comments: Site Reviews plugin (not published - just in backend)
Links: Pretty Links
Access credentials (wp-admin) will be provided after hiring


Not Needed:
No translation work (I'll handle this myself)
No audio recording (I'll handle this myself)
No automation/custom development beyond what's needed (this is an MVP)


MVP
MVP with one example you can decide to show me the results.


Timeline
Completion within 2 weeks preferred.


Application

Please briefly address the following in your proposal:

Experience with the Elementor Pro Theme Builder
Experience with Polylang (multilingual setup)
Experience with Site Reviews or similar rating/comment plugins with image upload
Estimated time and fixed-price quote

I specialize in the Elementor Pro Theme Builder and multilingual configurations.
